Two groups carry architectural weight beyond this page: the `cluster_30` / `cluster_20` MMseqs2 columns pre-compute the material for leakage-safe splits, and the paired `st_*` state columns implement an explicit missing-data semantics ("observed / missing / reported-as-absent") that both the benchmark layer and the explorer's distance model consume. Full column-by-column documentation belongs to the schema page.

Sources: [data/README.md](data/README.md#L28-L37)

## Layer 2 — Source-Level Dataset Loaders (zhanglab/)

The `zhanglab/` package preserves the three original data sources as full lifecycle PyTorch `Dataset` classes: `DB1Dataset` (LLPSDB v2), `DB2Dataset` (laboratory notebooks), and `DB3Dataset` (RNAPSEC). Each class downloads upstream archives, validates the expected file layout, filters by system type, embeds proteins/nucleic acids/conditions through the Layer-3 embedding plane, persists the result as AnnData (`.h5ad`), and supports multiple train/test split strategies. These loaders therefore form the bridge between raw downloads and the `(x, c, y)` tensors of the model layers — and they keep per-*source* identity, which the merged per-*system* tables in Layer 1 deliberately collapse.

> [!TIP]
> A key boundary: the laboratory-notebook source (db2) is **not** included in the merged `data/` tables. The two record planes overlap but are not identical — `data/` is a merged benchmarking view, while `zhanglab/` loaders can yield records (and embeddings) that never enter the system-level tables.

Sources: [zhanglab/db1.py](zhanglab/db1.py#L42-L90), [data/README.md](data/README.md#L21-L24), [README.md](README.md#L39-L48)

## Layer 3 — Embedding and Configuration Plane

Two files at the repository root define the embedding plane. `meta_config.py` declares a Pydantic model, `MetaEmbeddingConfig`, with three validated slots — one per tuple element — and a factory, `create_meta_config()`, that benchmark and dataset code instantiate. `meta_embed.py` implements the actual encoders: `seq2esmc_dict()` runs ESM Cambrian (`Synthyra/ESMplusplus_large`, 600M) with a choice of pooling over residue positions, `seq2mtdp_dict()` loads the MTDP model with a T5 tokenizer, and `seqs2features29()` computes a 29-dimensional handcrafted physicochemical vector adapted from RNAPSEC.

| Config slot | Allowed values | Field default | Factory default |
|---|---|---|---|
| `protein_embedding` | `esmc`, `mtdp`, `rnapsec_protein`, `seq2ind`, `seq2onehot` | `esmc` | `mtdp` |
| `dna_rna_embedding` | `rnapsec_rna`, `dictionary` | `dictionary` | `dictionary` |
| `condition_embedding` | `droppler`, `rnapsec_condition`, `rnapsec_condition_class` | `droppler` | `droppler` |

Each slot is enforced by a `field_validator` with a closed set of names, so an invalid embedding choice fails at configuration time rather than mid-training. Note the deliberate asymmetry in the table above: the Pydantic field default and the factory default differ for the protein slot — code constructing configs via `create_meta_config()` gets `mtdp`, while constructing `MetaEmbeddingConfig()` directly gets `esmc`.

> [!TIP]
> The `MTDP/` folder ships **empty** in the repository — it is a runtime placeholder. `seq2mtdp_dict()` loads weights from `./MTDP/models/UniProtKB/UniProtKB.bin` and a tokenizer from `./MTDP/MTDP_tokenizer/` at call time, so MTDP embeddings require acquiring those assets separately; the `esmc` path needs only a HuggingFace checkpoint.

Sources: [meta_config.py](meta_config.py#L5-L41), [meta_embed.py](meta_embed.py#L48-L77), [meta_embed.py](meta_embed.py#L86-L150)

## Layer 4 — Benchmark Execution Layer

The two top-level task scripts standardize the canonical benchmarks over the source-level datasets. `task1.py` implements outcome prediction: it builds a `DB1Dataset` with a `create_meta_config(...)` selection, concatenates `x` and `c` into one feature matrix, standardizes it, applies a split via `get_idx_split(split_method=...)`, tunes an AdaBoost classifier with Optuna over 5-fold cross-validated AUROC, and reports AUROC, AUPRC, Cohen's kappa, and MCC via swanlab. `task2.py` trains **PhaseCVAE**, a conditional variational autoencoder for condition inference, on `DB3Dataset` slices — extracting protein, RNA, and condition tensors from the AnnData `obsm` store and carving stratified train/test loaders for phase-diagram grids.

The search space is declared centrally in `params_all.yaml`: seven system names, seven split strategies (random plus six condition-stratified variants), three protein methods, two DNA/RNA methods, three condition methods, and three tasks. The grid's composability is a direct consequence of the `(x, c, y)` contract and the validated config slots — every axis of the YAML maps one-to-one onto a parameter of the code path.

Sources: [task1.py](task1.py#L53-L100), [task2.py](task2.py#L1-L17), [task2.py](task2.py#L41-L100), [params_all.yaml](params_all.yaml#L1-L32)

## Layer 5 — Generative Model Families

Two generative stacks coexist, sharing the same conditional-UNet denoiser *pattern* but differing in the space in which diffusion operates. The **Discrete** stack diffuses sequences directly in categorical token space: `DiscreteMarginalTransition` builds one-step transition matrices `Q_t` from a learned amino-acid marginal (`data/train_marginal_x.pt`, 21 classes), the 1D conditional UNet in `protein_diffusion_model.py` injects conditions through `ConditionalEmbedding`/`LabelEmbedding` alongside sinusoidal time embeddings, and the `Trainer` in `training.py` orchestrates training with DDIM sampling (50 steps, 50-sample ensembles) and a `Evaluator` backed by a BLOSUM artifact. The **ldm** stack instead first compresses sequences: the JTAE autoencoder — a transformer with Performer attention and positional encoding — produces a latent `z` on which Gaussian diffusion runs, denoised by the conditional 1D UNet in `unet_conditional_model.py`, with a self-contained minimal variant in `ldm/ldm_minimal/`.

```mermaid
flowchart TB
    subgraph S1["Discrete/ — categorical diffusion"]
        A1["x₀ one-hot, 21 classes"] -->|"forward"| A2["Q_t from<br/>train_marginal_x.pt"]
        A2 --> A3["1D conditional UNet<br/>per-token logits"]
    end
    subgraph S2["ldm/ — latent diffusion"]
        B1["sequence embeddings"] --> B2["JTAE encoder<br/>(Performer attention)"]
        B2 --> B3["latent z"] -->|"Gaussian diffusion"| B4["conditional UNet denoiser"]
    end
```

| Dimension | Discrete/ | ldm/ |
|---|---|---|
| Diffusion space | token categories (21-way) | continuous latent (JTAE) |
| Forward process | categorical transitions from data marginal | Gaussian noise |
| Denoiser | 1D UNet + time/condition/label embeddings | 1D UNet + time/condition/label embeddings |
| Compression stage | none | JTAE autoencoder |
| Minimal variant | — | `ldm/ldm_minimal/` |
| Evaluation | `Evaluator` with BLOSUM scores | — |

The mathematical treatment of the marginal transitions, the denoiser internals, and the JTAE architecture each have dedicated Deep Dive pages; architecturally, the point to retain is that both stacks consume the same embedded-condition inputs as Layer 4, differing only in `x`-space representation.

Sources: [Discrete/Discrete_marginal_transition.py](Discrete/Discrete_marginal_transition.py#L4-L29), [Discrete/protein_diffusion_model.py](Discrete/protein_diffusion_model.py#L1-L16), [Discrete/training.py](Discrete/training.py#L25-L67), [ldm/JTAE/jtae_.py](ldm/JTAE/jtae_.py#L16-L60), [ldm/unet_conditional_model.py](ldm/unet_conditional_model.py#L17-L59)

## The records_space Subsystem: Explorer and Build Pipeline

`records_space/` is a self-contained subsystem with a two-sided output. Its **scripts** side (`rs01`–`rs17` numbered build stages, plus Colab driver scripts under `colab/`) produces the merged record tables from the six sources and the material for the map; its **site** side is static, browser-only HTML — the explorer (`index.html`), the negatives page (`negatives/index.html`), and embedded binary arrays in `export/`. The record map itself is a t-SNE over a weighted composite distance: protein embedding similarity (weight 0.40), nucleic-acid features (0.15), conditions (0.35), and buffer/additives (0.10), with unreported values treated as their own state rather than imputed — mirroring the `st_*` semantics of the Layer-1 schema.

| Distance block | Weight | Content |
|---|---:|---|
| protein | 0.40 | ESMC-600M layer-18 embedding (z-score, PCA to 64d, cosine) |
| nucleic acid | 0.15 | presence/class/name/length/concentration/fold features |
| conditions | 0.35 | protein concentration, pH, temperature, salts, crowders |
| buffer & additives | 0.10 | buffer and additive families |

The distance model and the site build pipeline each have dedicated pages in the Records Space Explorer section of this catalog; for the architecture, the essential fact is this subsystem's dual role as both the *origin* of the merged data tables and the *producer* of the interactive frontend.

Sources: [records_space/README.md](records_space/README.md#L8-L17), [records_space/README.md](records_space/README.md#L70-L77), [data/README.md](data/README.md#L41-L46)

## Recommended Reading Path

With the layer map established, the catalog's Deep Dive section can be traversed top-down through the same layers. The schema of the records you just saw is detailed next in [Condition-Level Record Schema](7-condition-level-record-schema); the benchmark layer unfolds in [Outcome Prediction Baselines](8-outcome-prediction-baselines), [Condition Inference with PhaseCVAE](9-condition-inference-with-phasecvae), and [Split Strategies and Metrics](10-split-strategies-and-metrics). The embedding plane is expanded in [Embedding Configuration Matrix](11-embedding-configuration-matrix), [Protein and Nucleic Acid Embeddings](12-protein-and-nucleic-acid-embeddings), and [Condition Feature Engineering](13-condition-feature-engineering). The generative stacks are treated mathematically across [Discrete Diffusion Foundations](14-discrete-diffusion-foundations) through [Latent Diffusion with JTAE](17-latent-diffusion-with-jtae), and the explorer subsystem in [Record Map Distance Model](19-record-map-distance-model) and [Site Build Pipeline](21-site-build-pipeline). For hands-on entry points before diving deep, return to [Quick Start](2-quick-start) and [Loading Records by System](3-loading-records-by-system).


# Condition-Level Record Schema



This page is the field-level reference for OpenPhase's core data product: the **condition-level record**. Every benchmark, embedding, and generative model in the repository consumes the same unit of observation — one experimental condition of one phase-separation experiment, stored as one row of `data/<system>/records.tsv`. Here you will learn what a record represents, the exact column groups it contains, how missing values are encoded, how the binary and saturation-concentration schema variants differ, and how the schema materializes as a DataFrame through the `openphase_systems` loader.

## What a "Condition-Level Record" Means

A record is **one experimental condition** of a single-protein phase-separation experiment with its outcome — a binary label (phase separation or not) or, for the saturation-concentration system, a measured concentration value. The granularity decision matters: the same protein appears many times (1,163 sequences span 7,490 records in the protein-only system), and the *condition* is what varies between rows. Conceptually each record decomposes into a protein at the center, an optional nucleic acid treated as a condition, physico-chemical conditions, buffer/additives, plus an outcome and provenance that ride along but are not themselves conditions.

Sources: [data/README.md](data/README.md#L3-L4), [records_space/README.md](records_space/README.md#L3-L4), [rslib.py](records_space/colab/rslib.py#L3)

```mermaid
flowchart TB
    R["One record = one experimental condition"]
    R --> ID["Identity / provenance<br/>record_id · source · paper · uniprot · protein_name<br/>seq_len · sequence_state · system_id"]
    R --> M["Construct descriptors<br/>mutation · fusion · cleaved · ptm"]
    R --> C["Physico-chemical conditions<br/>log10_protein_conc_uM · pH · temp_C · salts<br/>ionic strength · crowders (PEG/Ficoll/Dextran/Glycerol)"]
    R --> B["Buffer & additives<br/>buf_* and add_* 0/1 flags"]
    R --> N["Nucleic acid (optional)<br/>na_class · na_len_log10 · na_conc_log10<br/>na_* sequence and fold features"]
    R --> O["Outcome<br/>label · morphology · phase_state<br/>or readout_class · log10_value_uM · scan_axis"]
    C -. "each value column pairs with a state column" .-> ST["st_protein_conc · st_pH · st_temp · …"]
```

## The Four Systems and Their Tables

The **system** of a record is defined as the set of its components *without* concentrations — a nucleic acid, if present, is a condition (the `na_*` columns), not a component that defines a new table. Each system lives in its own folder as a tab-separated table, and `data/systems.tsv` carries the same counts broken down per source. The binary pool totals 10,663 records and the csat pool 776, giving the 11,439 records that the records-space explorer visualizes.

| folder | system | records | sequences | UniProt | papers | positive / negative |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| `data/protein/` | protein only | 7,490 | 1,163 | 311 | 364 | 4,416 / 3,074 |
| `data/protein_RNA/` | protein + RNA | 2,511 | 241 | 85 | 125 | 1,751 / 760 |
| `data/protein_DNA/` | protein + DNA | 662 | 99 | 42 | 41 | 446 / 216 |
| `data/protein_csat/` | saturation concentration | 776 | 42 | 3 | 2 | no binary label |

Sources: [data/README.md](data/README.md#L6-L13), [data/systems.tsv](data/systems.tsv#L1-L5), [records_space/README.md](records_space/README.md#L3)

The records were merged from upstream sources: LLPSDB v2 (split into `LLPSDB_v2_phase_diagram`, `LLPSDB_v2_site`, and `LLPSDB_v2` in the `source` column), LLPSense, RNAPSEC, the `PhaSepDB3_pilot_LLM` extraction, and — for csat — `Bremer2022` and `Ausserwoger2025`. The archived loaders `zhanglab/db1.py`, `db2.py`, `db3.py` build one dataset per *source*, whereas these tables merge per *system*; notably, the laboratory-notebook records (db2) are deliberately **not** included in the merged tables.

Sources: [data/systems.tsv](data/systems.tsv#L2-L5), [data/README.md](data/README.md#L21-L24), [openphase_systems.py](openphase_systems.py#L10)

## Anatomy of the Schema: Column Groups

Every `records.tsv` shares one header layout; the groups below are the canonical partition documented in `data/README.md` and confirmed by the raw files. Note that `system` appears in identity — but it is **inserted by the loader at read time** (position 1), not stored in the file. Also note the pairing convention: each numeric condition column sits directly next to its `st_<shortname>` state column (e.g., `log10_protein_conc_uM` → `st_protein_conc`, `temp_C` → `st_temp`).

| group | columns | semantics |
|---|---|---|
| identity | `record_id`, `system`*, `source`, `paper`, `uniprot`, `protein_name`, `seq_len`, `sequence_state`, `system_id`, `mutation`, `fusion`, `cleaved`, `ptm` | *who and where*: provenance + construct state |
| outcome | `label`, `morphology`, `phase_state`; csat: `readout_class`, `log10_value_uM`, `scan_axis` | *what happened* |
| split groups | `cluster_30`, `cluster_20` | MMseqs2 clusters at 30 % / 20 % identity, 80 % coverage |
| conditions | `log10_protein_conc_uM`, `pH`, `temp_C`, `MgCl2_mM`, `NaCl_mM`, `KCl_mM`, `ionic_strength_mM`, `PEG1k`, `PEG6k`, `PEG20k`, `Ficoll`, `Dex40`, `Dex70`, `Glycerol` | the experimental condition vector (crowders in per cent as reported) |
| buffer / additives | `buf_*` (8 buffer families), `add_*` (12 additive classes) | 0/1 multi-hot flags |
| missing-value state | `st_*` next to each condition | `obs` / `miss` / `zero` / `rt`; `none` / `other` for buffer & additive |
| nucleic acid | `na_class`, `na_len_log10`, `na_conc_log10`, `na_to_protein_ratio_log10`, `na_charge_ratio_log10`, `na_gc`, `na_purine`, `na_maxrun`, `na_g4`, `na_mfe_per_nt`, `na_paired_frac`, `na_len_source`, `na_homopolymer`, `na_name_*`, `na_has_sequence` | the nucleic-acid condition block |
| link | `binary_record_with_same_protein` | connects csat rows to binary records of the same protein |

\* `system` is injected by `load_system`, not present on disk.

Sources: [data/README.md](data/README.md#L26-L38), [data/protein/records.tsv](data/protein/records.tsv#L1-L3), [rslib.py](records_space/colab/rslib.py#L19-L24), [rs01_build_inputs.py](records_space/scripts/rs01_build_inputs.py#L37)

A concrete row makes the pairing tangible. The first protein-system record (`llpsdb2:PS00000010`, LAF-1) reads: `label=1`, `morphology=liquid`, `readout_class=binary`, then `log10_protein_conc_uM=0.60206` with `st_protein_conc=obs`, `pH=7.4` with `st_pH=obs`, `temp_C=22.0` with `st_temp=rt` (room temperature, not a measured value), `MgCl2_mM=0.0` with `st_MgCl2=zero` (author explicitly reported absence), and a run of `0` flags for unused crowders.

Sources: [data/protein/records.tsv](data/protein/records.tsv#L2-L3)

## The `st_*` Missing-Value Encoding

This is the schema's most important design decision: **an unreported value is empty and flagged in its `st_*` column — never imputed.** The state vocabulary distinguishes four epistemic situations for each condition dimension:

| `st_*` value | meaning | upstream origin |
|---|---|---|
| `obs` | a numeric value was observed and stored | default when a value exists |
| `miss` | not reported anywhere | value is empty |
| `zero` | author explicitly reported the component as absent | `absent_from_reported_*` status codes |
| `rt` | only "room temperature" stated; `temp_C` recorded as 22 | `room_temperature_unspecified` |

Buffer and additive columns use a slightly different pair: `st_buffer` ∈ {`obs`, `other` (free text present but no vocabulary hit), `miss` (no text at all)} and `st_additive` ∈ {`obs`, `none` (buffer text exists but no additives found), `miss`}. The derivation is deterministic — the state mapper converts the upstream status strings (`absent_from_reported_*` → `zero`, `room_temperature_unspecified` → `rt`) into the codes above.

Sources: [data/README.md](data/README.md#L33-L38), [rs01_build_inputs.py](records_space/scripts/rs01_build_inputs.py#L101-L108), [rs01_build_inputs.py](records_space/scripts/rs01_build_inputs.py#L111-L114)

> [!TIP]
> **Missing ≠ not applicable.** For the nucleic-acid block, a record without any nucleic acid is a *legitimate value* (`na_class=none`), not missing data — the `na_len_log10`/`na_conc_log10`/`na_ratio_log10` columns are then "not applicable", which downstream distance computations treat as a full dissimilarity rather than a missingness penalty. Confusing these two emptinesses is the classic integration error with this schema.

Sources: [rslib.py](records_space/colab/rslib.py#L10-L12), [rs01_build_inputs.py](records_space/scripts/rs01_build_inputs.py#L17)

## Outcome Columns: Binary vs Saturation-Concentration Variants

Both variants share one header, but the outcome block reinterprets itself. In the three binary systems, `label` ∈ {0, 1}, `readout_class` is the constant `"binary"`, and `morphology`/`phase_state` describe the observed condensate. In `protein_csat`, `label` is empty, `readout_class` enumerates scan positions — `dilute`, `csat_boundary`, `dilute_linescan`, `cloud_point`, `dense` — and `log10_value_uM` + `scan_axis` (a `temp` or `conc` scan) carry the quantitative readout. The `binary_record_with_same_protein` column then links each csat row back to binary records of the same protein, so the two pools can be joined without fragile name matching.

| column | binary systems | protein_csat |
|---|---|---|
| `label` | 1 = phase separation, 0 = none | empty (no binary label) |
| `readout_class` | `binary` | `dilute`, `csat_boundary`, `dilute_linescan`, `cloud_point`, `dense` |
| `log10_value_uM` | empty | log₁₀ of measured concentration |
| `scan_axis` | empty | `temp` or `conc` (which variable the scan swept) |
| `morphology` / `phase_state` | observed condensate morphology / phase | `n/a` |
| linkage | — | `binary_record_with_same_protein` |

Sources: [data/README.md](data/README.md#L29-L30), [data/protein_csat/records.tsv](data/protein_csat/records.tsv#L2-L3), [data/protein/records.tsv](data/protein/records.tsv#L2), [rs01_build_inputs.py](records_space/scripts/rs01_build_inputs.py#L5-L6)

## Identity and Provenance Design

The schema deliberately **excludes sequence text, language-model embeddings, and free-text source fields**: sequences are identified by `uniprot` + `seq_len` alone, and `sequence_state` records *how* each construct sequence was resolved (e.g., `row_construct_fasta`, `verified_SI_name_conflict`). Provenance is compact and typed: `record_id` follows a `source:row` convention (`llpsdb2:PS00000010`, `bremer_temp:0`), `source` is the controlled vocabulary of the six upstream datasets, and `paper` carries a prefixed identifier (`pmid:29064502`, `doi:10.1038/...`). `system_id` is a hash of the component set — two rows sharing it are the same physical mixture. Finally, `cluster_30`/`cluster_20` precompute sequence-similarity groups so leakage-aware splits are a group-by, not a recomputation. Because the tables are a processed benchmarking view built from source databases with heterogeneous licences, they are not a substitute for the sources themselves.

Sources: [data/README.md](data/README.md#L28-L29), [data/README.md](data/README.md#L40-L43), [data/protein/records.tsv](data/protein/records.tsv#L1-L2), [data/protein_csat/records.tsv](data/protein_csat/records.tsv#L2)

> [!TIP]
> **`system_id` is your join key for mixture identity, `cluster_30`/`cluster_20` for leakage control.** When grouping records by experiment or splitting train/test, never split on `record_id` — it is unique per condition by design, so a naive random split places sister conditions of the same paper and protein on both sides. Group on `system_id` (same mixture) or the cluster columns (same sequence family) instead; the split strategies page covers the corresponding split methods.

Sources: [data/README.md](data/README.md#L30-L31)

## Loading the Schema Programmatically

The `openphase_systems` module is a thin, read-only view over the four tables. `list_systems()` returns `data/systems.tsv` verbatim (counts plus per-source breakdown); `load_system(name)` reads one table and **inserts the `system` column at position 1**; the optional `source` argument filters rows whose `source` string starts with a prefix (e.g., `"RNAPSEC"`); `load_all()` returns a dict of DataFrames for all or a selected subset; unknown system names raise a `ValueError` listing valid choices.

| function | signature | returns / behavior |
|---|---|---|
| `list_systems` | `() -> pd.DataFrame` | one row per system: records, sequences, UniProt, papers, sources, labels |
| `load_system` | `(system, source=None) -> pd.DataFrame` | table rows + injected `system` column; `source` prefix filter; index reset |
| `load_all` | `(systems=None) -> Dict[str, pd.DataFrame]` | dictionary `system name → records DataFrame` |

```python
from openphase_systems import list_systems, load_system, load_all
list_systems()
rna = load_system("protein_RNA")                      # all 2,511 records
rnapsec = load_system("protein_RNA", source="RNAPSEC")  # 1,141 rows only
everything = load_all()                               # {"protein": …, "protein_RNA": …, …}
```

Sources: [openphase_systems.py](openphase_systems.py#L27-L45), [data/README.md](data/README.md#L15-L19)

## How the Schema Flows Through the Repository

The tables are the downstream edge of the records-space build and the upstream edge of everything else: benchmark tasks read `label`/`outcome` columns for prediction baselines, the split machinery consumes `cluster_30`/`cluster_20`, condition feature engineering turns the condition + `na_*` + `buf_*`/`add_*` blocks into model inputs, and the record-map distance model computes inter-record distances directly from the condition, nucleic-acid, and buffer blocks — with `st_*` states deciding whether a dimension contributes an absolute difference, a missingness penalty, or nothing.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    SRC["Upstream sources<br/>LLPSDB v2 · LLPSense · RNAPSEC<br/>PhaSepDB3 pilot · Bremer 2022 · Ausserwöger 2025"]
    RS["records-space build<br/>(state codes, vocabularies)"]
    SRC --> RS
    RS --> T1["data/protein/records.tsv"]
    RS --> T2["data/protein_RNA/records.tsv"]
    RS --> T3["data/protein_DNA/records.tsv"]
    RS --> T4["data/protein_csat/records.tsv"]
    T1 --> LD["openphase_systems<br/>load_system / load_all"]
    T2 --> LD
    T3 --> LD
    T4 --> LD
    LD --> B["Outcome Prediction Baselines"]
    LD --> S["Split Strategies (cluster_30 / cluster_20)"]
    LD --> F["Condition Feature Engineering"]
    LD --> D["Record Map Distance Model"]
```

Sources: [data/README.md](data/README.md#L45), [rs01_build_inputs.py](records_space/scripts/rs01_build_inputs.py#L16)

**Where to go next.** For a guided walkthrough of the loader in practice, continue to [Loading Records by System](3-loading-records-by-system); for how condition columns become model inputs, see [Condition Feature Engineering](13-condition-feature-engineering); for leakage-aware usage of the cluster columns, see [Split Strategies and Metrics](10-split-strategies-and-metrics); for the label-driven baselines, see [Outcome Prediction Baselines](8-outcome-prediction-baselines); and for the distance semantics over this exact schema, see [Record Map Distance Model](19-record-map-distance-model).

# Outcome Prediction Baselines



This page documents **Task 1 — Phase Outcome Prediction**, the first of OpenPhase's canonical benchmarks. The goal is to learn a function from a system's *components* (protein, RNA, or DNA sequences, denoted **x**) and its *experimental conditions* (pH, salt, temperature, crowding, concentration, denoted **c**) to a binary phase-separation outcome **y ∈ {0, 1}** — with one regression variant that predicts a continuous saturation readout. All four baseline implementations live in a single orchestration module, `task1.py`, which is the reference script for this task; the sibling `task2.py` belongs to the condition-inference benchmark and is covered separately in [Condition Inference with PhaseCVAE](9-condition-inference-with-phasecvae).

Sources: [README.md](README.md#L56-L62), [README.md](README.md#L119-L125), [task1.py](task1.py#L1-L19)

## The Task Contract

The benchmark is defined in the repository README under *Canonical Tasks*: given components **x** (protein/RNA sequences) and conditions **c** (environmental factors), predict whether the system undergoes liquid–liquid phase separation. The README's *Standardized Benchmarking* section commits each task to three artifacts — standardized train/test splits, baseline models, and evaluation metrics — and names `task1.py` as their documentation entry point. This page describes exactly those three artifacts for the outcome-prediction task.

Sources: [README.md](README.md#L49-L62), [README.md](README.md#L119-L125)

## Architecture: From Archived Loaders to Baselines

The baselines never touch the merged per-system TSV tables (`data/<system>/records.tsv`) exposed by `openphase_systems.py`. Instead they run on the **archived per-source loaders** in `zhanglab/`, which reproduce the original datasets used to train the published models: `DB1Dataset` (LLPSDB v2), `DB2Dataset` (laboratory-notebook phase diagrams), and `DB3Dataset` (RNAPSEC). Each loader follows an identical self-managing lifecycle — download raw archives, parse and filter, embed, and cache everything in an AnnData `.h5ad` file keyed by system and embedding method.

Sources: [openphase_systems.py](openphase_systems.py#L1-L13), [db1.py](zhanglab/db1.py#L27-L50), [db2.py](zhanglab/db2.py#L21-L43), [README.md](README.md#L43-L47)

Two dataset methods form the stable interface every baseline consumes. `get_tensor()` returns the embedded feature tensors, with an **arity that varies by system composition** — `protein(1)` returns `(x, c, y)`, while multi-protein or nucleic-acid systems return extra sequence tensors ahead of `(c, y)`. `get_idx_split(split_method=...)` returns train/test index arrays for one of seven split strategies (80/20 by default). The baselines are written to be composition-agnostic: `baseline_rnapsec` unpacks with `*x, c, y = system_dataset.get_tensor()` and concatenates all sequence tensors along the last axis, so the same code path serves single-protein and complex systems alike.

Sources: [db1.py](zhanglab/db1.py#L504-L572), [db1.py](zhanglab/db1.py#L422-L433), [task1.py](task1.py#L26-L37)

> [!TIP]
> When embedding a system, AnnData keys are written with f-strings (e.g. `f'c_{condition_embedding_model}'` at db1.py#L392) but two read sites construct the condition key as a *plain string* without the `f` prefix (`db1.py#L445`, `db1.py#L521`). In `get_idx_split` that lookup is harmless dead code — `c` is never used after assignment — but in `get_tensor` it is live. If you wire a new condition embedding method into the baselines, verify the actual `obsm` key naming in the cached `.h5ad` first.

The following module-interaction diagram shows the full data flow for the benchmark:

```mermaid
graph LR
    CFG["meta_config.py :: MetaEmbeddingConfig"] --> DB1["zhanglab/db1.py :: DB1Dataset - LLPSDB v2"]
    CFG --> DB2["zhanglab/db2.py :: DB2Dataset - lab notebooks"]
    DB1 -->|"get_tensor + get_idx_split"| B1["baseline_rnapsec :: AdaBoost + Optuna"]
    DB1 -->|"get_tensor + get_idx_split"| B2["baseline_droppler :: selfatt_RRN neural net"]
    DB1 -->|"get_tensor + get_idx_split"| B3["protein1_condformer :: encoder + classifier head"]
    B3 -->|"frozen encoder checkpoint"| B4["protein1_regression :: MSE regression head"]
    DB2 -->|"IDR subset, continuous y"| B4
    B1 --> M["sklearn metrics :: AUROC / AUPRC / Kappa / MCC"]
    B2 --> M
    B3 --> M
    B4 --> M
    M --> L["swanlab experiment logging"]
```

Sources: [meta_config.py](meta_config.py#L38-L40), [db1.py](zhanglab/db1.py#L404-L420), [task1.py](task1.py#L17-L19)

## The Baseline Suite

`task1.py` implements four baselines that form a deliberate difficulty ladder: two classical/external models that treat the problem as a fixed feature-vector task, one native deep model trained end-to-end on OpenPhase's embedding system, and one transfer-learning regression variant that extends the deep model from binary outcomes to a continuous saturation readout.

| Baseline | System scope | Dataset | Model | Protocol | Defining hyperparameters |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `baseline_rnapsec` | Any DB1 system (flat vectors) | `DB1Dataset` | `AdaBoostClassifier` over `DecisionTreeClassifier` stumps | Optuna study, 32 trials, 5-fold CV on macro-OVR AUROC | `max_depth` ∈ {5–10, None}, `learning_rate` ∈ {0.5–2.5}, `random_state=30` |
| `baseline_droppler` | Any DB1 system, condition method must be `droppler` | `DB1Dataset` | External `SA.selfatt_RRN` (20 aa features, 14 condition slots, 10 heads) via `NNwrapper` | 10 epochs, batch 1024 | `lr=3e-3`, `weight_decay=1e-4` |
| `protein1_condformer` | `protein(1)` only (asserted) | `DB1Dataset` | `Protein1SystemEncoder` + `PhaseClassificationHead` | Full-batch BCE, 1000 epochs, best-AUROC checkpointing | `embed_dim=256`, `dropout=0.5`, Adam `lr=7e-4`, `wd=7e-6` |
| `protein1_regression` | `DB2Dataset` IDR subset (continuous csat) | `DB2Dataset` | Frozen CondFormer encoder + `PhaseRegressionHead` | Full-batch MSE, 1000 epochs, best-MSE checkpointing | Adam `lr=3e-4`, `wd=5e-6`, 50/50 split |

Sources: [task1.py](task1.py#L58-L103), [task1.py](task1.py#L142-L226), [task1.py](task1.py#L242-L348), [task1.py](task1.py#L351-L463)

### `baseline_rnapsec` — the Optuna-tuned tree ensemble

The flow is: load tensors → `StandardScaler` on the concatenated `[x, c]` matrix → Optuna search over AdaBoost depth/learning-rate with 5-fold cross-validation scored by macro one-vs-rest AUROC → refit the best configuration → evaluate on the held-out split. All four classification metrics plus the experiment's configuration are pushed to swanlab in a single flat dictionary, making runs directly comparable across embedding and split choices.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A["DB1Dataset get_tensor"] --> B["concat x tensors + StandardScaler"]
    B --> C["Optuna study: 32 trials"]
    C --> D["5-fold CV, macro OVR AUROC"]
    D --> E["refit best AdaBoost"]
    E --> F["predict on test split"]
    F --> G["AUROC, AUPRC, Kappa, MCC to swanlab"]
```

Sources: [task1.py](task1.py#L40-L55), [task1.py](task1.py#L58-L103)

### `baseline_droppler` — the sequence-aware neural baseline

This baseline reproduces the Droppler architecture against OpenPhase data. Sequences are converted to integer indices over the 20 canonical amino acids (unknown characters map to 0) and zero-padded to a common length with `pad_sequence`, so the model sees raw token sequences rather than precomputed embeddings. Conditions are carved out of the condition tensor by column position — temperature, concentration, salt, crowding, pH — and scaled with a pickled scaler shipped from the original Droppler codebase (`clip` disabled). The function hard-asserts `condition_embedding == "droppler"` because the 14-column condition layout it slices depends on that encoding.

Sources: [task1.py](task1.py#L105-L139), [task1.py](task1.py#L147-L185), [task1.py](task1.py#L202-L226)

### `protein1_condformer` — the native deep baseline

Restricted to the `protein(1)` system by assertion, this baseline composes a `Protein1SystemEncoder` (which fuses protein and condition embeddings into a 256-dim system representation) with a `PhaseClassificationHead`. Training is deliberately simple — full-batch forward/backward with binary cross-entropy for 1000 epochs — followed by a per-epoch full test evaluation. The best checkpoint by AUROC is saved under a filename that encodes both the system and the split method, `./task1/models/condformer_{system_name}_{split_method}_best.pth`; this naming convention is what the regression driver later exploits for transfer experiments.

Sources: [task1.py](task1.py#L242-L277), [task1.py](task1.py#L280-L336), [task1.py](task1.py#L338-L348)

### `protein1_regression` — transfer to saturation concentration

The regression variant loads the `DB2Dataset` IDR subset, whose labels are continuous phase-separation measurements rather than binary outcomes (the DB2 docstring distinguishes the binary `CoREST`/`RGG` subsets from continuous `IDR`). It rebuilds a `Protein1SystemEncoder`, loads encoder weights from a CondFormer classification checkpoint, **freezes them**, and trains only a `PhaseRegressionHead` under MSE loss on a 50/50 split. Predictions are exported as `pred_vs_true_{model_name}.csv` into `./task1/results/`, and a seaborn jointplot visualizes true-vs-predicted alignment.

Sources: [db2.py](zhanglab/db2.py#L21-L43), [db2.py](zhanglab/db2.py#L107-L109), [task1.py](task1.py#L351-L401), [task1.py](task1.py#L415-L463)

> [!TIP]
> Watch the encoder input-dimension coupling when moving between the two deep baselines: the classification path sizes `protein_dim` as 29 (`rnapsec_protein`) / 1280 (`mtdp`) / **1024** (anything else, i.e. `esmc`) at task1.py#L267-L272, but the regression transfer path uses **1152** for that same fallback branch at task1.py#L384-L389. A checkpoint trained in one path cannot be loaded into the other unless the dimension branch matches its training provenance.

### Choosing a baseline

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    Q{"What is the target and system?"}
    Q -->|"binary y, protein + RNA/DNA systems, flat features"| RNA["baseline_rnapsec: trees + Bayesian HPO"]
    Q -->|"binary y, raw sequence tokens, droppler conditions"| DR["baseline_droppler: selfatt_RRN"]
    Q -->|"binary y, protein(1) only, native embeddings"| CF["protein1_condformer"]
    CF -->|"continuous csat readout, reuse encoder"| RG["protein1_regression on DB2 IDR"]
```

Sources: [task1.py](task1.py#L120-L126), [task1.py](task1.py#L252-L258)

## Embedding Configuration Coupling

Every baseline receives its feature representation through `create_meta_config(protein=..., dna_rna=..., condition=...)`, a thin factory over the pydantic-validated `MetaEmbeddingConfig`. The allowed value sets are enforced at construction time: protein ∈ {`esmc`, `mtdp`, `rnapsec_protein`, `seq2ind`, `seq2onehot`}, DNA/RNA ∈ {`rnapsec_rna`, `dictionary`}, condition ∈ {`droppler`, `rnapsec_condition`, `rnapsec_condition_class`}. Defaults are `mtdp` / `dictionary` / `droppler`. Because `DB1Dataset` caches one `.h5ad` per system and re-embeds automatically when a requested embedding key is missing, changing a baseline's embedding arguments transparently triggers recomputation on the next run.

| Method argument | Accepted values | Dimension consumed by deep baselines |
|---|---|---|
| `protein` | `esmc`, `mtdp`, `rnapsec_protein`, `seq2ind`, `seq2onehot` | 29 / 1280 / 1024 (classification) or 1152 (regression fallback) |
| `dna_rna` | `rnapsec_rna`, `dictionary` | selected inside `get_tensor` per nucleic-acid system |
| `condition` | `droppler`, `rnapsec_condition`, `rnapsec_condition_class` | 4 (`rnapsec_condition`) or 14 (otherwise) |

Sources: [meta_config.py](meta_config.py#L5-L40), [task1.py](task1.py#L267-L272), [task1.py](task1.py#L384-L389), [db1.py](zhanglab/db1.py#L601-L628)

The full option matrix, per-model engineering details, and cost characteristics are documented in [Embedding Configuration Matrix](11-embedding-configuration-matrix), [Protein and Nucleic Acid Embeddings](12-protein-and-nucleic-acid-embeddings), and [Condition Feature Engineering](13-condition-feature-engineering).

## Splits and Evaluation Protocol

Split behavior is delegated entirely to the dataset layer: `get_idx_split` supports `random`, plus six stratified variants (`phase_label_stratified`, `temperature_stratified`, `component_concentration_stratified`, `ionic_strength_stratified`, `crowding_agent_stratified`, `pH_stratified`), all 80/20, with conditions discretized into bins (quantile bins for concentration and ionic strength, fixed bins for temperature and pH) before stratification. Passing an unknown method raises a `ValueError` that enumerates the full list. The regression driver at the bottom of `task1.py` demonstrates the intended ablation pattern: it sequentially calls `protein1_regression` against all seven CondFormer checkpoints (one per split strategy), producing a transfer matrix over split regimes. A complete treatment of split semantics and metric interpretation belongs to [Split Strategies and Metrics](10-split-strategies-and-metrics).

Sources: [db1.py](zhanglab/db1.py#L422-L502), [task1.py](task1.py#L466-L477)

Metric computation is uniform across the three classification baselines and deliberately redundant — two threshold-free ranking metrics and two discrete-agreement metrics:

| Metric | Measures | Computed via | Uses |
|---|---|---|---|
| AUROC | Ranking quality, macro one-vs-rest | `roc_auc_score` | predicted probabilities |
| AUPRC | Precision–recall trade-off under imbalance | `average_precision_score` | predicted probabilities |
| Cohen's Kappa | Chance-corrected agreement | `cohen_kappa_score` | hard labels (`predict` or `>= 0.5`) |
| MCC | Balanced binary correlation | `matthews_corrcoef` | hard labels (`>= 0.5`) |
| MSE / R² | Regression error and explained variance | `mean_squared_error`, `r2_score` | continuous IDR readout |

Sources: [task1.py](task1.py#L86-L102), [task1.py](task1.py#L205-L226), [task1.py](task1.py#L309-L315), [task1.py](task1.py#L432-L456)

All runs log under a single swanlab project (`ConditionPhase`), initialized once at module scope before the driver invocations, so every baseline's configuration — system, split, and all three embedding methods — is recorded alongside its metrics.

Sources: [task1.py](task1.py#L94-L102), [task1.py](task1.py#L466-L477)

## Running the Baselines

There is no CLI wrapper: `task1.py` is executed as a script whose module-level driver section runs the regression transfer experiments. To run a different baseline, import the function and supply the four configuration arguments — for example `baseline_rnapsec("protein(1)", "random", "rnapsec_protein", "dictionary", "rnapsec_condition")`. Note two environment expectations before executing: the module appends `./scripts` and `./droppler` to `sys.path` at import time (the `model1`, `SA`, and `NNWrappers` modules referenced by the deep baselines resolve from those paths), and GPU usage is auto-selected via `torch.device("cuda" if ...)` inside each deep baseline. First runs will also trigger dataset downloads — LLPSDB v2 archives for DB1, a Google Drive XLSX for DB2 — cached under `./data/DB1` and `./data/DB2`.

```python
from task1 import baseline_rnapsec, protein1_condformer

# Classical ensemble on any system, any embedding configuration
baseline_rnapsec(
    system_name="protein(1) + RNA",
    split_method="phase_label_stratified",
    protein_method="esmc",
    dna_rna_method="dictionary",
    condition_method="rnapsec_condition",
)

# Native deep baseline, protein(1) only
protein1_condformer("protein(1)", "random", "mtdp", "dictionary", "droppler")
```

Sources: [task1.py](task1.py#L17-L19), [task1.py](task1.py#L58-L68), [task1.py](task1.py#L167-L171), [task1.py](task1.py#L254-L258), [task1.py](task1.py#L466-L477), [db1.py](zhanglab/db1.py#L54-L59), [db2.py](zhanglab/db2.py#L111-L120)

If you need the record schema behind the system names passed as `system_name`, see [Condition-Level Record Schema](7-condition-level-record-schema); for building datasets from the loaders themselves, see [Building Source Datasets with Loaders](5-building-source-datasets-with-loaders).

## Summary and Next Steps

The outcome-prediction benchmark gives you a reproducible difficulty ladder: **tree ensembles with Bayesian HPO** as the sanity floor, a **reproduced external neural baseline** for continuity with prior work, a **native CondFormer** as the condition-aware reference model, and a **transfer-learning regression head** that turns classification machinery into a saturation-concentration predictor — all sharing one embedding configuration, one split interface, and one metric/logging protocol. With outcomes covered, the natural continuations are learning the inverse problem in [Condition Inference with PhaseCVAE](9-condition-inference-with-phasecvae), understanding exactly how the split regimes reshape difficulty in [Split Strategies and Metrics](10-split-strategies-and-metrics), and tuning the feature representations these baselines consume via [Embedding Configuration Matrix](11-embedding-configuration-matrix).


# Condition Inference with PhaseCVAE



This page documents the second canonical benchmark of OpenPhase: **condition inference**. Where the outcome-prediction baseline (see [Outcome Prediction Baselines](8-outcome-prediction-baselines)) answers *"will this system phase-separate under these conditions?"*, condition inference inverts the question: *"which experimental conditions drive a given protein–RNA system into phase separation?"* The reference implementation is `task2.py`, which trains **PhaseCVAE** — a Conditional Variational Autoencoder — on the DB3 protein–RNA phase-diagram dataset and then sweeps a 2D condition grid (protein concentration × RNA concentration) to reconstruct the phase boundary of a single molecular system.

Sources: [task2.py](task2.py#L1-L4), [README.md](README.md#L56-L67)

## The Inverse Problem: Outcome Prediction vs. Condition Inference

OpenPhase defines three canonical tasks, and task 2 is explicitly the conditional counterpart of task 1: *"Inferring the potential experimental conditions (c) that lead to a specific phase separation outcome, enabling rational experimental design"* ([README.md](README.md#L63-L64)). Instead of using conditions as input features to predict an outcome label, PhaseCVAE treats **conditions as the thing to be inferred** — the model must reconstruct the phase outcome from component embeddings plus a candidate condition vector, and the condition vector itself becomes the search space for inference.

This framing has a concrete consequence for the model design: PhaseCVAE consumes **both** the molecular components (protein and RNA embeddings) **and** a condition vector, and it is trained with a compound objective that couples condition–outcome consistency (a phase-prediction loss) to a variational reconstruction objective (reconstruction + KL terms). The result is a model that behaves as a score function over the condition plane, which is exactly what the grid-based phase-diagram inference exploits later in the pipeline.

Sources: [task2.py](task2.py#L355-L358), [task2.py](task2.py#L186-L192)

## Data Foundation: DB3 and Its AnnData Embedding Store

PhaseCVAE is trained exclusively on **DB3**, the RNAPSEC-derived benchmark. `DB3Dataset` (`zhanglab/db3.py`) self-describes as *"a preprocessed resource derived from RNAPSEC (Chin et al. 2024)... focusing on the phase behavior of protein-RNA systems"* and ships a three-stage lifecycle: **download → process → embed**.

1. **Download**: pulls `rnapsec.xlsx` directly from the upstream `ycu-iil/RNAPSEC` GitHub repository when the raw file is absent.
2. **Process**: parses experimental metadata into a unified schema — phase label, system composition (`protein(1) + RNA`), UniProt ID, protein sequence, component concentration, nucleic acid type/sequence, temperature (with `RT → 25` normalization), ionic strength (unit-normalized to mM), buffer pH, and crowding agent — and saves complete-case tables (`rnapsec_1514.txt`, `rnapsec_no_missing_1298.txt`).
3. **Embed**: maps phase morphology to binary labels (`{"liquid": 1, "solid": 1, "gel": 1, "solute": 0}` — any condensed phase counts as positive) and writes all representations into a single `.h5ad` AnnData store under deterministic `obsm` keys: `y`, `x_{protein_method}`, `x_rna_{dna_rna_method}`, and `c_{condition_method}`.

Sources: [db3.py](zhanglab/db3.py#L17-L38), [db3.py](zhanglab/db3.py#L96-L122), [db3.py](zhanglab/db3.py#L124-L202), [db3.py](zhanglab/db3.py#L204-L248)

The embedding methods are selected through `MetaEmbeddingConfig` (`meta_config.py`), a Pydantic-validated triple `(protein_embedding, dna_rna_embedding, condition_embedding)`. Task 2 instantiates it with `create_meta_config(protein="mtdp", dna_rna="dictionary", condition="rnapsec_condition")` (`task2.py` L466-468). Note the interaction with the downstream code: the condition embedding `c_rnapsec_condition` is a multi-column numeric matrix, and the **last two columns** are treated by task 2 as the *(protein concentration, RNA concentration)* pair — this is the only 2D slice the condition-inference experiment operates on. The full condition-embedding options (including Droppler's 14-dimensional encoding: 10 temperature bins + concentration + ionic strength + crowding + pH) are covered in [Condition Feature Engineering](13-condition-feature-engineering) and [Embedding Configuration Matrix](11-embedding-configuration-matrix).

Sources: [meta_config.py](meta_config.py#L5-L41), [task2.py](task2.py#L52-L112), [meta_embed.py](meta_embed.py#L588-L599), [meta_embed.py](meta_embed.py#L529-L586)

## The PhaseCVAE Contract

The model class itself is imported from `model2` (task 2 appends `./scripts` to `sys.path` at line 8), so what the repository guarantees publicly is the **call contract** — observable through every call site in `task2.py`:

| API element | Signature / behavior | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| Constructor | `PhaseCVAE(protein_dim, nucleic_dim, condition_dim, latent_dim=64, hidden_dim=128)` | [task2.py](task2.py#L304-L310) |
| Training/inference entry | `compute_loss(x_protein, x_rna, c, y, alpha, beta, gamma) → (loss_dict, y_pred)` | [task2.py](task2.py#L355-L358) |
| Loss dictionary keys | `recon_loss`, `kl_loss`, `phase_loss`, `total_loss` | [task2.py](task2.py#L186-L192) |
| Output | `y_pred` — a continuous score thresholded at 0.5 for binary metrics | [task2.py](task2.py#L399-L405) |
| Dataset wrapper | `SelectedSystemDataset(x_protein, x_rna, c_protein_rna, y, indices)` — tensor tuples of exactly these four arrays | [task2.py](task2.py#L93-L96) |

The loss decomposition makes the "condition inference" objective explicit. Each batch loss is a weighted sum of three verifiable components:

| Component | Key | Weight (default) | Role in the objective |
|---|---|---|---|
| Reconstruction | `recon_loss` | `alpha = 10.0` | Variational reconstruction of the input representation |
| Regularization | `kl_loss` | `beta = 0.1` | KL divergence keeping the 64-dim latent well-behaved for sampling/inference |
| Phase consistency | `phase_loss` | `gamma = 5.0` | Alignment between predicted phase score `y_pred` and the observed label `y` |
| Total | `total_loss` | — | Optimized quantity; also the model-selection criterion |

Sources: [task2.py](task2.py#L355-L371), [task2.py](task2.py#L263-L268)

The dataflow below is reconstructed strictly from this verified contract (constructor dimensions, loss keys, and the `compute_loss` signature) — the internal layer wiring of `model2.py` is not part of the tracked tree in this snapshot:

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    XP["x_protein (B, D_p)<br/>protein embedding"] --> ENC["Encoder<br/>→ latent z (64-d)"]
    XR["x_rna (B, D_r)<br/>RNA embedding"] --> ENC
    ENC --> KL["kl_loss (β=0.1)"]
    ENC --> DEC["Decoder<br/>hidden 128"]
    C["c (B, 2)<br/>protein + RNA concentration"] --> DEC
    DEC --> RECON["recon_loss (α=10)"]
    DEC --> Y["y_pred (B,)"]
    Ytrue["y (B,)<br/>phase label"] --> PH["phase_loss (γ=5)"]
    Y --> PH
    RECON & KL & PH --> T["total_loss"]
```

## End-to-End Pipeline in `task2.py`

The script's `__main__` block chains eight verifiable steps, from dataset construction to a logged, checkpointed phase diagram:

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    A["create_meta_config<br/>mtdp / dictionary / rnapsec_condition"] --> B["DB3Dataset(root='../data', download=True)<br/>download → process → embed"]
    B --> C["db3_ann = db3[:]  (AnnData obsm store)"]
    C --> D["select_by_protein_nucleic_acid<br/>Protein ID 'P35637' + nucleic acid 'MAPT'"]
    D --> E["create_selected_dataset_and_loader<br/>StratifiedShuffleSplit, test_size = 0.5"]
    E --> F["create_condition_grid<br/>30 × 30 points, margin 0.25"]
    F --> G["grid_label_knn_inference<br/>k = 5 pseudo-labels for grid"]
    G --> H["train_phase_cvae<br/>100 epochs, Adam, lr 1e-2"]
    H --> I["per-epoch: grid_inference_same_system<br/>+ plot_grid_same_system"]
    I --> J["SwanLab logging<br/>+ best-test-loss checkpoint"]
```

Step-by-step, with the exact verified behavior:

1. **System selection** — `select_by_protein_nucleic_acid` filters the DB3 frame by `Protein ID` and/or `Nucleic acid`; the demo run isolates the Tau protein (`P35637`) with the RNA transcript `MAPT`, producing a single-system cohort whose condition ranges define the inference plane ([task2.py](task2.py#L228-L252), [task2.py](task2.py#L474-L479)).
2. **Data splitting** — `create_selected_dataset_and_loader` performs a `StratifiedShuffleSplit` (test proportion 0.5, seed 42) over the selected samples, wraps both halves in `SelectedSystemDataset` loaders (batch size 1024), and additionally emits `grid_range_dict` (min/max per condition axis) and `phase_diag_dict` (condition–label arrays per split) ([task2.py](task2.py#L52-L112)).
3. **Condition grid** — `create_condition_grid` builds a `num_points × num_points` meshgrid over the observed concentration ranges, extended by a fractional `margin` on each side (0.1 default, 0.25 in the demo run) so the inferred phase boundary can be drawn slightly beyond the data support ([task2.py](task2.py#L115-L145), [task2.py](task2.py#L492)).
4. **Grid pseudo-labels** — `grid_label_knn_inference` labels every grid point by k-nearest-neighbor voting (k=5) over the combined train+test condition–label reference points; these labels let the grid inference evaluate the model's phase loss at arbitrary condition points ([task2.py](task2.py#L203-L225), [task2.py](task2.py#L493-L499)).
5. **Grid inference** — `grid_inference_same_system` runs the trained model over all 900 grid points with the component embeddings held fixed, collecting per-point `y_pred` plus all four loss values — this is what produces the rendered phase diagram and its diagnostic heatmaps ([task2.py](task2.py#L148-L200)).

> [!TIP]
> The phase diagram is a diagram of **one molecular system, many conditions** — not many systems. `grid_inference_same_system` receives a single protein/RNA embedding pair (the first training sample, `x_protein_sample[0]` / `x_rna_sample[0]` at task2.py L502 and L512-513) and sweeps only the 2D concentration plane. To generate a diagram for a different system, change the selection at step 1 — the grid machinery itself is system-agnostic.

Sources: [task2.py](task2.py#L462-L499), [task2.py](task2.py#L148-L200)

## Training Loop, Metrics, and Checkpointing

`train_phase_cvae` is a single-device (CUDA when available) training loop with standard yet precisely pinned engineering choices. Dimensions (`protein_dim`, `nucleic_dim`, `condition_dim`) are read from the first batch rather than hardcoded, so swapping embedding methods only changes what the loaders emit ([task2.py](task2.py#L298-L310)).

| Setting | Value | Mechanism |
|---|---|---|
| Optimizer | `Adam`, initial LR `1e-2` | [task2.py](task2.py#L313) |
| LR schedule | `ReduceLROnPlateau(patience=10, factor=0.5)` stepped on mean **test** total loss | [task2.py](task2.py#L314-L316), [task2.py](task2.py#L441) |
| Gradient clipping | `clip_grad_norm_(max_norm=1.0)` every step | [task2.py](task2.py#L362) |
| Epochs (demo) | 100 | [task2.py](task2.py#L514) |
| Latent / hidden dims | 64 / 128 | [task2.py](task2.py#L304-L310) |
| Model selection | Best mean test `total_loss`; checkpoint saves epoch, model and optimizer state to `./task2/models` | [task2.py](task2.py#L444-L456) |
| Logging | SwanLab project `condition_phase`: per-epoch loss decomposition, accuracy, ROC AUC, ROC/PR curves, and the rendered grid phase diagram | [task2.py](task2.py#L407-L438) |

Quality is measured each epoch on both splits: predictions are binarized at a 0.5 threshold for `accuracy_score`, and raw scores feed `roc_auc_score` — the same evaluation axes used by the other benchmarks (see [Split Strategies and Metrics](10-split-strategies-and-metrics) for the cross-task split/metric protocol). Because the test loss drives both LR scheduling and checkpointing, the split produced in step 2 is not merely an evaluation formality: it is the control signal for the whole run.

Sources: [task2.py](task2.py#L341-L405), [task2.py](task2.py#L407-L459), [task2.py](task2.py#L493-L520)

## Running the Benchmark Yourself

The minimal invocation mirrors the `__main__` block:

```python
from zhanglab.db3 import DB3Dataset
from meta_config import create_meta_config
from model2 import PhaseCVAE, SelectedSystemDataset  # resolved via ./scripts on sys.path

meta_config = create_meta_config(protein="mtdp", dna_rna="dictionary", condition="rnapsec_condition")
db3 = DB3Dataset(root="../data", name="DB3", embedding_config=meta_config, download=True)
```

When adapting the demo, verify these integration points first — they are the ones where the demo's implicit assumptions bite:

| Symptom / risk | Root cause (verified in code) | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `ModuleNotFoundError: model2` | `task2.py` resolves `model2` and `meta_plot` via `sys.path.append("./scripts")` (L8, L18-19); that directory is outside the tracked top-level tree in this snapshot | Ensure `scripts/model2.py` exists locally before running; the class contract above is the compatibility surface |
| Missing `obsm` keys `x_esmc_normed` / `x_rna_rnapsec_rna_normed` | The demo reads standardized `_normed` copies, while a fresh DB3 build with the `mtdp`/`dictionary` config writes `x_mtdp` / `x_rna_dictionary` (db3.py L225-L227); `_normed` keys are produced by `get_scaled_and_umap(..., save_normed=True)` | Run the scaling step (`get_scaled_and_umap`, task2.py L27-L49) to add `_normed` copies, or point `create_selected_dataset_and_loader` at the raw keys |
| `KeyError` on `c_rnapsec_condition` column slice | The loader takes `obsm[condition_embedding][:, -2:]` — the condition matrix must have ≥ 2 columns ordered so the last two are the component concentrations | Regenerate the condition embedding with the same `rnapsec_condition` method used at embed time |
| Degenerate 2D grid (single point per axis) | The selected system cohort has constant protein or RNA concentration, collapsing `grid_range_dict` ranges | Broaden the `select_by_protein_nucleic_acid` filter or shrink the system constraint |

Sources: [task2.py](task2.py#L6-L24), [task2.py](task2.py#L27-L49), [task2.py](task2.py#L79-L85), [db3.py](zhanglab/db3.py#L223-L228)

## Where This Fits in the Benchmark Suite

Task 2 is the middle rung of OpenPhase's condition-aware ladder. Task 1 (`task1.py`) predicts outcomes from concatenated condition features with classical baselines (AdaBoost with Optuna-tuned depth/learning-rate, plus a Droppler-style self-attention network) — a strictly feed-forward use of `c` ([task1.py](task1.py#L40-L48), [task1.py](task1.py#L58-L103)). Task 2 closes the loop by making the condition vector the object of study through a generative-style latent model. The generative machinery that OpenPhase uses for the third task — designing new sequences rather than new conditions — lives in the diffusion stack and is covered from [Discrete Diffusion Foundations](14-discrete-diffusion-foundations) onward; the record-level schema both tasks consume is documented in [Condition-Level Record Schema](7-condition-level-record-schema), and the broader system architecture in [Architecture Overview](6-architecture-overview).


# Split Strategies and Metrics



This page documents how OpenPhase partitions its benchmark datasets into train/test sets and which metrics quantify model performance on the canonical tasks. The split machinery is centralized in the archived dataset loaders under `zhanglab/` — most notably `DB1Dataset.get_idx_split()`, which exposes **seven named split strategies** driven by condition columns — while the task scripts (`task1.py`, `task2.py`) define the metric suites, model selection rules, and experiment logging. Everything here applies to the **Outcome Prediction** and **Condition Inference** benchmarks; generative-model evaluation is covered separately in [Sequence Generation Evaluation](18-sequence-generation-evaluation), and the record schema that feeds the stratification columns is described in [Condition-Level Record Schema](7-condition-level-record-schema).

Sources: [db1.py](zhanglab/db1.py#L422-L502), [README.md](README.md#L49-L55)

## Where Splits Live in the Benchmark Stack

The benchmark flow is deliberately simple: each task script instantiates a dataset with an embedding configuration, requests a split by *name*, indexes its feature matrices with the returned indices, then trains, evaluates, and logs. The split step is the only component that is aware of experimental conditions; models and metrics remain agnostic to how the partition was made.

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A["DB1Dataset / DB2Dataset / DB3Dataset<br/>(embedded AnnData .h5ad)"] --> B["get_idx_split(split_method)"]
    B --> C["train_idx, test_idx"]
    C --> D["task1.py baselines<br/>rnapsec · droppler · condformer"]
    C --> E["task2.py PhaseCVAE"]
    D --> F["AUROC · AUPRC · Kappa · MCC<br/>MSE · R²"]
    E --> G["Accuracy · ROC AUC<br/>recon/KL/phase losses"]
    F --> H["SwanLab logging<br/>+ checkpoint per split_method"]
    G --> H
```

The `split_method` string travels with the experiment: it is logged to SwanLab as a first-class field and is baked into checkpoint filenames, so every reported number is traceable to both an embedding configuration and a split strategy.

Sources: [task1.py](task1.py#L58-L102), [task2.py](task2.py#L462-L520), [meta_config.py](meta_config.py#L38-L41)

## The Split Engine: `get_idx_split`

`DB1Dataset.get_idx_split(split_method, seed)` is the canonical entry point. It re-reads the system's embedded AnnData file (`{system}.no_missing.h5ad`), extracts the label vector `y` plus six raw condition columns, and dispatches on `split_method` via a Python `match` statement. All strategies return a `(train_idx, test_idx)` tuple of NumPy index arrays; an unrecognized name raises a `ValueError` that echoes the full list of valid strategies, making the API self-documenting at the call site.

```python
train_idx, test_idx = system_dataset.get_idx_split(split_method="pH_stratified")
```

The optional `seed` parameter seeds both `torch.manual_seed` and `np.random.seed` before any sampling, which is the intended reproducibility hook. All stratified variants delegate the actual partitioning to `sklearn.model_selection.train_test_split` with a fixed `test_size=0.2`; only the `random` strategy does its own 80/20 cut via `np.random.permutation`.

Sources: [db1.py](zhanglab/db1.py#L422-L437), [db1.py](zhanglab/db1.py#L459-L462), [db1.py](zhanglab/db1.py#L497-L502)

> [!TIP]
> Inside `get_idx_split`, the condition key is built as `c_key = 'c_{self.embedding_config.condition_embedding}'` — a plain string literal, **not** an f-string (db1.py#L445). When reproducing splits against your own embedded h5ad files, ensure the `obsm` key matches what this lookup actually resolves to, or the `c` extraction will fail before any split logic runs.

## Anatomy of the Seven Split Strategies

The strategy family splits cleanly into two groups: one unconditioned baseline and six **condition-stratified** variants. The design goal is that each test set preserves the distribution of one specific experimental factor, so benchmark results measure generalization *across* that factor's values rather than within an uncontrolled random sample.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    S["get_idx_split(split_method)"] --> R["random"]
    S --> P["phase_label_stratified"]
    S --> T["temperature_stratified"]
    S --> CC["component_concentration_stratified"]
    S --> IS["ionic_strength_stratified"]
    S --> CA["crowding_agent_stratified"]
    S --> PH["pH_stratified"]
    R --> B1["np.random.permutation<br/>80/20"]
    P --> B2["stratify = Phase label<br/>test_size 0.2"]
    T --> B3["pd.cut fixed °C bins<br/>→ stratify"]
    CC --> B4["pd.qcut 5 quantiles<br/>→ stratify"]
    IS --> B5["pd.qcut 5 quantiles<br/>→ stratify"]
    CA --> B6["stratify = binary Yes/No<br/>test_size 0.2"]
    PH --> B7["pd.cut fixed pH bins<br/>→ stratify"]
```

| Strategy | Stratification variable | Binning method | Bins / classes | Test size |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `random` | none | `np.random.permutation` | — | 20% |
| `phase_label_stratified` | `Phase label` | raw labels | per-label | 20% |
| `temperature_stratified` | mean temperature | `pd.cut` fixed edges | −25–25, 25–50, 50–75, 75–100 °C | 20% |
| `component_concentration_stratified` | component concentration | `pd.qcut` quantiles | low → high (5) | 20% |
| `ionic_strength_stratified` | ionic strength | `pd.qcut` quantiles | low → high (5) | 20% |
| `crowding_agent_stratified` | `Crowding agent` | raw binary values | Yes / No | 20% |
| `pH_stratified` | buffer pH | `pd.cut` fixed edges | (2.5, 5.5], (5.5, 8.5], (8.5, 11.5] | 20% |

Each stratified branch logs the resulting bin counts (e.g., `temperature_bins.value_counts()`) and, for quantile methods, the computed bin edges — useful diagnostics when a sparse bin makes the stratification fragile.

Sources: [db1.py](zhanglab/db1.py#L458-L498)

## How Stratification Columns Are Derived

Before dispatch, the six stratification inputs are parsed out of the AnnData dataframe with string operations tailored to each column's messy experimental format. Temperature values arrive as comma-separated lists and are averaged (`str.split(', ', expand=True).astype(float).mean(axis=1)`); concentrations and ionic strengths keep only the leading numeric token and fill missing entries with `0` (`fillna(0)`); pH extracts the second whitespace-separated token; crowding agent is used as-is.

The binning choice is the analytically interesting part: **fixed-edge `pd.cut`** is used for temperature and pH, where physically meaningful ranges exist (e.g., the (2.5, 5.5], (5.5, 8.5], (8.5, 11.5] pH windows), while **data-driven `pd.qcut` quintiles** are used for component concentration and ionic strength, whose distributions are skewed and best balanced by quantiles labeled `low` through `high`. Quantile edges are returned (`retbins=True`) and logged, so the exact numeric boundaries of every run are recoverable from its console output.

Sources: [db1.py](zhanglab/db1.py#L444-L455), [db1.py](zhanglab/db1.py#L469-L478), [db1.py](zhanglab/db1.py#L493-L495)

## Dataset-Specific Splits: DB2 and DB3

Only DB1 implements a split *method* on the dataset object. The other two loaders leave partitioning to their task scripts, with a distinctly different ratio — **50/50** instead of 80/20 — reflecting their use in transfer and per-system phase-diagram experiments where within-system coverage matters more than a large training pool.

| Dataset | Split call | Stratified on | Ratio | Where |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| DB1 (LLPSDBv2) | `get_idx_split(split_method=…)` | 6 selectable factors | 80/20 | [db1.py](zhanglab/db1.py#L422-L502) |
| DB2 (IDR subset) | `train_test_split(idx, test_size=0.5, random_state=42)` | no | 50/50 | [task1.py](task1.py#L376-L381) |
| DB3 (RNAPSEC) | `StratifiedShuffleSplit(n_splits=1, test_size=0.5, random_state=42).split(x_protein, y)` | phase label `y` | 50/50 | [task2.py](task2.py#L88-L91) |

The DB3 split in `task2.py` is the condition-inference benchmark's protocol: after selecting a protein–RNA system (e.g., `P35637` + `MAPT`), the split stratifies on the binary phase label so train and test phase diagrams have matching class balance, and both partitions are simultaneously packaged into `SelectedSystemDataset` dataloaders plus phase-diagram arrays for grid visualization.

Sources: [task1.py](task1.py#L365-L381), [task2.py](task2.py#L78-L111), [task2.py](task2.py#L462-L476)

## The Metric Suite

Metrics are task-shaped. Outcome-prediction baselines report a four-metric classification panel computed with scikit-learn; the IDR transfer experiment reports regression quality; the PhaseCVAE condition-inference loop reports accuracy plus AUC and a decomposed loss vector.

### Outcome Prediction (task1.py, classification)

All three baselines — the AdaBoost `rnapsec` model, the self-attention `droppler` model, and the `condformer` encoder/classifier pair — report the identical panel:

| Metric | Function | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| AUROC | `roc_auc_score(…, multi_class="ovr", average="macro")` | primary selection metric for condformer |
| AUPRC | `average_precision_score(…, average="macro")` | threshold-free, reported alongside AUROC |
| Cohen's Kappa | `cohen_kappa_score(y_test, y_pred)` | chance-corrected agreement at 0.5 threshold |
| MCC | `matthews_corrcoef(y_test, y_pred)` | balanced correlation at 0.5 threshold |

For the droppler and condformer baselines, hard predictions are derived by thresholding probabilities at **0.5** (`y_probs >= 0.5`); the rnapsec baseline uses `predict()` directly and reads `predict_proba(…)[:, 1]` for the ranking metrics.

Sources: [task1.py](task1.py#L86-L102), [task1.py](task1.py#L205-L226), [task1.py](task1.py#L304-L312)

### IDR Regression (task1.py, transfer)

The regression head is evaluated each epoch with `mean_squared_error` and `r2_score` on the test half; the **best checkpoint is the one with lowest test MSE**, and a final pass re-loads that head to emit `y_true`/`y_pred` CSV pairs per transferred encoder.

| Metric | Function | Role |
|---|---|---|
| MSE | `torch.nn.functional.mse_loss` / `mean_squared_error` | training loss and checkpoint criterion |
| R² | `r2_score` | variance explained, logged per epoch |

Sources: [task1.py](task1.py#L414-L439), [task1.py](task1.py#L448-L456)

### Condition Inference (task2.py, PhaseCVAE)

The VAE loop binarizes continuous predictions at 0.5 and reports `accuracy_score` and `roc_auc_score` for both partitions each epoch. In parallel it tracks the weighted loss decomposition — reconstruction (`alpha=10.0`), KL (`beta=0.1`), and phase prediction (`gamma=5.0`) — because the scheduler and best-checkpoint rule operate on the **mean total test loss**, not on a classification metric.

| Signal | Computation | Used for |
|---|---|---|
| accuracy / AUC | threshold 0.5 on `y_pred` | per-epoch quality trend |
| recon / KL / phase losses | `model.compute_loss(...)` components | `ReduceLROnPlateau` + best-model selection |
| ROC & PR curves | `plot_roc_pr_curves(...)` images | SwanLab visual logging |

Sources: [task2.py](task2.py#L398-L409), [task2.py](task2.py#L417-L441), [task2.py](task2.py#L514-L519)

## Model Selection and Split-Aware Experiment Logging

Every benchmark run ties its artifacts back to the split. The condformer loop evaluates the full test set **every epoch**, logs the metric panel via SwanLab, and keeps a running best keyed on AUROC — saving encoder and classifier state dictionaries plus all four metrics into `condformer_{system_name}_{split_method}_best.pth`. Because the split method is embedded in the filename, the repository's transfer experiment can sweep a single classifier across all seven DB1 partitions and compare downstream regression quality per split.

Sources: [task1.py](task1.py#L314-L330), [task1.py](task1.py#L470-L476)

The rnapsec and droppler baselines additionally wrap training in an **Optuna study** (32 trials, `n_jobs=32`) whose objective is 5-fold cross-validated macro-OVR AUROC on the *training split only* — the test indices produced by `get_idx_split` are never touched during hyperparameter search, keeping the reported test metrics honest.

Sources: [task1.py](task1.py#L40-L48), [task1.py](task1.py#L79-L84)

All three logging sites record a common metadata block — `system_name`, `split_method`, and the three embedding methods — so any SwanLab dashboard row uniquely identifies a (dataset, split, embedding, metric) cell of the benchmark grid. The full space of embedding options that combine with these splits is tabulated in [Embedding Configuration Matrix](11-embedding-configuration-matrix).

Sources: [task1.py](task1.py#L94-L102), [task1.py](task1.py#L213-L226), [task2.py](task2.py#L320-L336)

> [!TIP]
> The checkpoint naming convention `condformer_{system}_{split}_best.pth` (task1.py#L329) is effectively the benchmark's comparison contract: seven split-tagged checkpoints already exist for the `protein(1)` system, and `protein1_regression` consumes them as frozen encoders. Preserve this naming if you add strategies, or downstream transfer sweeps will silently miss your runs.

## Reproducibility Notes and Practical Usage

A complete, reproducible benchmark cell is three lines of configuration:

```python
from meta_config import create_meta_config
from zhanglab.db1 import DB1Dataset

config = create_meta_config(protein="rnapsec_protein", condition="rnapsec_condition")
dataset = DB1Dataset(root="./data", name="DB1", system="protein(1)", embedding_config=config)
train_idx, test_idx = dataset.get_idx_split(split_method="pH_stratified", seed=42)
```

Three caveats follow directly from the code. First, `get_idx_split` **re-reads the h5ad on every call**, so a split is always consistent with the embeddings currently on disk rather than with an in-memory dataset — regenerate splits only after embeddings are finalized. Second, the `seed` argument is the only reproducibility control; when it is `None` (the task scripts' default), each call yields a fresh partition. Third, stratified splits can fail on systems whose binned factor has classes with fewer than two members, which is a plausible failure mode for the smaller `protein(2)`/`protein(3)` systems — the fixed pH and temperature bins in particular assume the LLPSDBv2 condition coverage documented in [Condition-Level Record Schema](7-condition-level-record-schema).

Sources: [db1.py](zhanglab/db1.py#L435-L448), [db1.py](zhanglab/db1.py#L460-L465), [task1.py](task1.py#L58-L77)

For a decision guide between strategies: use `random` as the variance floor, `phase_label_stratified` as the default classification benchmark, and the five condition-stratified variants when the research question concerns robustness to a specific environmental axis — the paired checkpoints let you quantify exactly how much each stratification choice costs or gains in AUROC, AUPRC, Kappa, and MCC.

Sources: [task1.py](task1.py#L309-L330), [task1.py](task1.py#L470-L476)

## Where to Go Next

Continue the benchmark track with [Outcome Prediction Baselines](8-outcome-prediction-baselines) for the model architectures behind the metric panel, and [Condition Inference with PhaseCVAE](9-condition-inference-with-phasecvae) for the loss-weighted VAE protocol. To see how these splits interplay with the embedding choices listed above, read [Embedding Configuration Matrix](11-embedding-configuration-matrix); for the complete hyperparameter surface that Optuna searches within, see [Hyperparameter Grid Reference](22-hyperparameter-grid-reference).


# Embedding Configuration Matrix



OpenPhase does not hard-code any single feature representation. Instead, every benchmark task selects its feature space through a **three-slot embedding configuration**: one slot for the protein component, one for the DNA/RNA component, and one for the experimental condition component. This page documents that matrix — the exact set of legal options per slot, the backend functions that implement each option, the dimensionality contracts they guarantee, and how the configuration is materialized into AnnData `obsm` keys and consumed by the benchmark tasks. The matrix is declarative: you name three strings, validators enforce legality, and a dispatcher layer turns those names into tensors.

Sources: [meta_config.py](meta_config.py#L1-L41), [meta_embed.py](meta_embed.py#L390-L430)

## The Three-Slot Contract: `MetaEmbeddingConfig`

The single source of truth for the matrix is `MetaEmbeddingConfig`, a Pydantic `BaseModel` with three fields and one validator per field. Each validator holds a closed set of allowed identifiers and rejects anything else with a `ValueError`, which makes invalid combinations fail at construction time rather than mid-training. The three fields are:

| Slot | Field | Default (class) | Default (factory) | Allowed values |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Protein | `protein_embedding` | `"esmc"` | `"mtdp"` | `esmc`, `mtdp`, `rnapsec_protein`, `seq2ind`, `seq2onehot` |
| DNA/RNA | `dna_rna_embedding` (Optional) | `"dictionary"` | `"dictionary"` | `rnapsec_rna`, `dictionary` |
| Condition | `condition_embedding` | `"droppler"` | `"droppler"` | `droppler`, `rnapsec_condition`, `rnapsec_condition_class` |

Note the deliberate divergence between the class-level defaults (`protein_embedding="esmc"`) and the convenience factory `create_meta_config(protein="mtdp", ...)`, whose signature defaults to MTDP. When you construct the config directly, you get ESM Cambrian; when you go through the factory, you get MTDP unless you override it. Choose one entry path and stay consistent across experiment sweeps to avoid silently comparing different protein spaces.

Sources: [meta_config.py](meta_config.py#L5-L41)

```mermaid
classDiagram
    class MetaEmbeddingConfig {
        +str protein_embedding = "esmc"
        +Optional~str~ dna_rna_embedding = "dictionary"
        +str condition_embedding = "droppler"
        +validate_protein_embedding(v) rejects outside 5-value set
        +validate_dna_rna_embedding(v) rejects outside 2-value set
        +validate_condition_embedding(v) rejects outside 3-value set
    }
    class create_meta_config {
        +protein="mtdp"
        +dna_rna="dictionary"
        +condition="droppler"
    }
    create_meta_config ..> MetaEmbeddingConfig : constructs
```

Sources: [meta_config.py](meta_config.py#L16-L41)

> [!TIP]
> Naming semantics matter: `rnapsec_*` options do **not** run a neural RNAPSEC checkpoint. They reproduce the RNAPSEC project's *handcrafted feature recipes* — 29 Biopython-derived protein descriptors and 97 MathFeature-derived RNA descriptors. The `rnapsec_protein` dispatcher branch literally calls the 29-dimensional ProtParam extractor, despite an inline comment suggesting an ESM fallback.

Sources: [meta_embed.py](meta_embed.py#L120-L134), [meta_embed.py](meta_embed.py#L419-L420)

## Options Grid: Backends, Dimensions, and Dependencies

Multiplying the validator sets gives the full configuration space: **5 protein × 2 DNA/RNA × 3 condition = 30 legal combinations** per system. Each combination resolves to a concrete backend function in `meta_embed.py` with a fixed output contract:

| Slot | Option | Backend | Output contract | External dependency |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| protein | `esmc` | `seq2esmc_dict` | One pooled vector per sequence (mean/max/sum/norm/prod/median) | `Synthyra/ESMplusplus_large` checkpoint (ESM Cambrian 600M) |
| protein | `mtdp` | `seq2mtdp_dict` | `(1280,)` float vector per sequence | Local `./MTDP/models/UniProtKB/UniProtKB.bin` + T5 tokenizer |
| protein | `rnapsec_protein` | `seqs2features29` | DataFrame `(n, 29)` | Biopython `ProteinAnalysis` |
| protein | `seq2ind` | `seqs2ind` | DataFrame `(n, 2048)` integer indices | None (pad or random-crop to 2048) |
| protein | `seq2onehot` | `seq2onehot` | ndarray `(n, 2048, 21)` | None (20 AA + `X` catch-all) |
| dna_rna | `dictionary` | inline logic | `(Series of unique integer indices, mapping dict)` | None |
| dna_rna | `rnapsec_rna` | `seqs2features97` | DataFrame `(n, 97)` | MathFeature toolkit via subprocess |
| condition | `droppler` | inline logic | DataFrame `(n, 14)` | None |
| condition | `rnapsec_condition` | inline logic | DataFrame `(n, 3 + k)` log-scale scalars | None |
| condition | `rnapsec_condition_class` | inline logic | DataFrame `(n, 3 + k)` categorical bins | None |

Two structural facts follow from this grid. First, the `seq2ind` and `seq2onehot` protein options are legal in the config but are **excluded from the benchmark hyperparameter grid** (`params_all.yaml` sweeps only `rnapsec_protein`, `esmc`, `mtdp`), reducing the swept protein axis to 3 options. Second, the DNA/RNA slot is only materialized for nucleic-acid systems; the dataset-level existence check treats the slot as satisfied (`True`) whenever the system has no nucleic acid, so the 30-combination space collapses gracefully for protein-only systems.

Sources: [meta_embed.py](meta_embed.py#L44-L117), [meta_embed.py](meta_embed.py#L318-L387), [meta_embed.py](meta_embed.py#L433-L459), [params_all.yaml](params_all.yaml#L17-L27), [zhanglab/db1.py](zhanglab/db1.py#L615-L620)

## Dispatcher Architecture

The matrix resolves through three dispatcher functions — `get_protein_embeddings`, `get_dna_rna_embeddings`, and `get_condition_embeddings` — each accepting the option string and branching to its backend. The dispatchers, not the callers, own the output normalization: protein dispatchers return a pandas `DataFrame` (one row per input sequence, order preserved), the DNA/RNA dispatcher returns a `(embeddings, mapping)` tuple, and the condition dispatcher returns a single `DataFrame` indexed like the input conditions.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    CFG["MetaEmbeddingConfig"] --> PE["get_protein_embeddings"]
    CFG --> NE["get_dna_rna_embeddings"]
    CFG --> CE["get_condition_embeddings"]
```
