To reproduce either artifact end-to-end, run the stages in this order (paths are relative to `records_space/`):

| Step | Command | Produces |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `colab/rs12_universe.py --data /content/rs12/data --out /content/rs12/out` (via `colab/run_universe.sh <session>`) | `data/universe/colab_out/universe.npz` + embedding shards |
| 2 | `python3 -I scripts/rs13_universe_export.py` | `explorer/universe_data.json` |
| 3 | `python3 -I scripts/rs14_pu_manifest.py` | `data/pu/pu_manifest.tsv`, `sets.json`, `pu_new_ids.tsv` |
| 4 | `colab/rs15_pu.py --data /content/rs13/data --out /content/rs13/out` (via `colab/run_pu.sh <session> [limit]`, optionally `RESUME_DIR=…`) | `data/pu/colab_out_nu/pu_map.npz` |
| 5 | `python3 -I scripts/rs16_build_pu.py` | `pu_page/index.html`, `page_fragment.html`, `summary.json` |
| 6 | `python3 -I scripts/rs17_build_site.py` | `site/records_space/negatives/index.html` (staged copy of step 5's standalone page) |

The `--limit N` flag on rs15 restricts how many `src=new` proteins are fetched and embedded — useful for smoke-testing the GPU path before committing to a full multi-hour run, since Colab sessions are capped at a 14,400-second execution timeout in both runners.

Sources: [rs15_pu.py](records_space/colab/rs15_pu.py#L23-L38), [run_universe.sh](records_space/colab/run_universe.sh#L36), [run_pu.sh](records_space/colab/run_pu.sh#L39), [rs16_build_pu.py](records_space/scripts/rs16_build_pu.py#L78-L84), [rs17_build_site.py](records_space/scripts/rs17_build_site.py#L95-L97)

# Site Build Pipeline


The `records_space/` folder ships three static pages to GitHub Pages: a home page, the records explorer, and a negatives/unlabelled-proteins map. None of them are hand-edited HTML — each is **assembled by a numbered Python script** that injects data blobs and JavaScript modules into HTML templates, then rs17 stages everything into a `site/` tree that mirrors the repository root one-to-one. This page explains how the build works end to end: what each assembler consumes and produces, the template-injection contract they all share, the Colab orchestration layer that feeds them, and the caveats around rebuilding the site from the committed files.

## What the Pipeline Produces
The published site is exactly three HTML entry points plus static assets: `index.html` (home, with the hero figure and two clickable system figures), `records_space/index.html` (the explorer), and `records_space/negatives/index.html` (negatives and unlabelled proteins). The README states that GitHub Pages serves these from the repository, and that the home page is built by `scripts/rs17_build_site.py` from `home_page/home_template.html`. The committed root `index.html` (171 lines) is verifiably the rendered template output — its head section is byte-for-byte the same markup that `home_template.html` defines, confirming the build products are checked into the repo rather than generated at deploy time.
Sources: [README.md](/records_space/README.md#L46-L48), [rs17_build_site.py](/records_space/scripts/rs17_build_site.py#L1-L8), [index.html](/index.html#L1-L10), [home_template.html](/records_space/home_page/home_template.html#L1-L12)

```
site/  (staging tree, mirrors repository root)
├── index.html                              ← rs17: home_template.html + hotspots + chips
├── assets/
│   ├── openphase-main.webp                 ← cwebp-encoded hero figure (q=88)
│   ├── openphase-wordmark.webp             ← cwebp-encoded transparent logo (q=92)
│   ├── fig-protein1-systems.webp           ← system figure A (2000×1793)
│   └── fig-multi-protein-systems.webp      ← system figure B (2000×1475)
├── records_space/
│   ├── index.html                          ← copy of explorer/records_space_explorer.html (rs05 output)
│   └── negatives/
│       └── index.html                      ← copy of pu_page/index.html (rs16 output)
```

## Architecture Overview
The build is a two-tier pipeline: heavy numerical work (embeddings, distances, t-SNE/UMAP) runs in ephemeral **Colab sessions** driven by zsh scripts that use a `colab` CLI, while all **page assembly runs locally** with pure-stdlib Python. Numbered `rsNN` scripts mark the stages: `rs01` prepares input tables from the Task 1 main table (10,663 binary records) and the csat pool (776 records); `rs02`/`rs03` compute embeddings and layouts on Colab; `rs05` packs the result into the self-contained explorer; `rs09` exports the "try your own experiment" data; `rs12`–`rs15` build the protein universe and negatives map; and `rs17` performs the final site staging.
Sources: [rs01_build_inputs.py](/records_space/scripts/rs01_build_inputs.py#L1-L17), [rs05_build_explorer.py](/records_space/scripts/rs05_build_explorer.py#L1-L7), [run_export.sh](/records_space/colab/run_export.sh#L1-L3), [run_universe.sh](/records_space/colab/run_universe.sh#L1-L4)

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    subgraph SRC[Source data]
        T1["Task 1 main table<br/>10,663 binary records"]
        CSAT["csat_features.tsv<br/>776 csat records"]
    end
    subgraph LOCAL[Local, stdlib only]
        RS01["rs01_build_inputs.py<br/>rs_records.tsv · rs_sequences.tsv"]
        RS10["rs10 · rs11<br/>example defs · tools table"]
        RS05["rs05_build_explorer.py"]
        RS16["rs16_build_pu.py"]
        RS17["rs17_build_site.py"]
    end
    subgraph COLAB[Colab sessions]
        RS0203["rs02 embed · rs03 distances<br/>t-SNE / UMAP · rs09 export"]
        RS12["rs12 universe (GPU)"]
        RS15["rs15 PU map (GPU)"]
    end
    EXP["explorer/<br/>records_space_explorer.html"]
    PU["pu_page/index.html"]
    SITE[("site/ staging tree")]
    GH[("GitHub Pages")]

    T1 --> RS01
    CSAT --> RS01
    RS01 -->|"data + code upload"| RS0203
    RS0203 -->|"records.bin · seqs.bin<br/>params.json · approx.json"| RS05
    RS10 --> RS05
    RS12 --> RS05
    RS15 --> RS16
    RS05 --> EXP
    RS16 --> PU
    EXP --> RS17
    PU --> RS17
    RS17 --> SITE --> GH
```

## The Three Page Assemblers
All three assemblers follow one pattern — read a template, substitute placeholders with generated content, emit both a fragment and a standalone file — but they operate at different pipeline stages and validate different invariants. rs05 is the data-heaviest (it embeds the full record table, five coordinate lenses, and binary export arrays), rs16 is the negatives page builder, and rs17 is the final packager that also encodes image assets and stitches the previously built pages into the staging tree.
Sources: [rs05_build_explorer.py](/records_space/scripts/rs05_build_explorer.py#L195-L215), [rs16_build_pu.py](/records_space/scripts/rs16_build_pu.py#L75-L83), [rs17_build_site.py](/records_space/scripts/rs17_build_site.py#L83-L95)

| Assembler | Inputs | Template | Placeholders | Outputs | Key validation |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `rs05_build_explorer.py` | `out/rs_plot_table.tsv`, `out/rs_coords.tsv`, `export/*` binaries, `explorer/examples/`, `tools_data.json`, `universe_data.json` | `explorer/explorer_template.html` | `/*__DATA__*/null` + 3 JS slots | `explorer/page_fragment.html`, `explorer/records_space_explorer.html` | `records.bin` concentration column cross-checked against the plot table, mismatch must be < 1% of rows |
| `rs16_build_pu.py` | Colab `pu_map.npz`, `pu_manifest.tsv`, `sets.json` | `pu_page/pu_template.html` | `/*__DATA__*/null` | `pu_page/page_fragment.html`, `pu_page/index.html`, `summary.json` | asserts every set has `role == "N"` (negatives only) |
| `rs17_build_site.py` | `home_template.html`, theme PNGs, built explorer/PU pages | `home_page/home_template.html` | `{{HS_B}}`, `{{HS_A}}`, `{{CHIPS_B}}`, `{{LOGO_W}}`, `{{LOGO_H}}` | whole `site/` tree | asserts each placeholder occurs **exactly once**; asserts source figures exist |

Sources: [rs05_build_explorer.py](/records_space/scripts/rs05_build_explorer.py#L154-L180), [rs16_build_pu.py](/records_space/scripts/rs16_build_pu.py#L31-L40), [rs17_build_site.py](/records_space/scripts/rs17_build_site.py#L83-L87)

## rs17: Home Page Assembly
rs17 begins with **asset preparation**. It copies the two session-produced system figures (`fig-multi-protein-systems.webp`, `fig-protein1-systems.webp`) into `home_page/figs/` and then into `site/assets/`, and shells out to the `cwebp` encoder to convert theme PNGs — the hero figure at quality 88 and the transparent wordmark at quality 92 with `alpha_q 100` to preserve the logo's alpha channel. This is the only point in the pipeline with an external binary dependency.
Sources: [rs17_build_site.py](/records_space/scripts/rs17_build_site.py#L21-L30)

The home page's signature feature is its **clickable system figures**. Hotspot geometry is authored as `(shape, geometry_in_native_pixels, href, tooltip)` tuples — 15 entries for the protein(1) figure (2000×1793) and 7 for the multi-protein figure (2000×1475). Each hotspot links into the explorer using its URL-hash parameters, so "FUS" opens `records_space/#protein=FUS`, a source circle opens `#hl=llpsense&na=none`, and the four lower-row panels filter by system type (`#na=none&csat=hide`, `#csat=only`, …). The seven multi-protein hotspots have no `href` and render as `.hs.off` spans with a "not built yet" tooltip.
Sources: [rs17_build_site.py](/records_space/scripts/rs17_build_site.py#L33-L71), [README.md](/records_space/README.md#L50-L59)

| Shape | Pixel geometry | Explorer link | Tooltip |
|---|---|---|---|
| rect | (52, 1158, 506, 1642) | `records_space/#na=none&csat=hide` | protein(1): protein only, 7,490 records |
| rect | (1493, 1158, 1947, 1642) | `records_space/#csat=only` | protein(1), Csat pool, 776 records |
| circle | (605, 365, r=172) | `records_space/#hl=llpsdb&na=none&csat=hide` | LLPSDB v2, protein only |
| circle | (1335, 150–700 box) | `records_space/#protein=FUS` | FUS: 836 records, 46 papers |
| rect (off) | (30, 165, 520, 720) | — (span, no link) | protein(2): 953 systems, 4,406 records |

Sources: [rs17_build_site.py](/records_space/scripts/rs17_build_site.py#L44-L68)

> [!TIP]
> The `box()` helper converts pixel geometry into percentage-based `left/top/width/height`, so hotspots are **resolution-independent**: the image scales fluidly with the viewport while the clickable regions stay locked to the figure's features, and no JavaScript is needed to reposition them on resize.

The substitution step is deliberately brittle: rs17 asserts each placeholder occurs exactly once in the template before replacing it, then writes `site/index.html`. The template itself supplies the responsive layout, light/dark theming (CSS custom properties plus a `localStorage`-persisted toggle), the P and N+U cards with dataset statistics, and a `?debug` query flag that adds a `body.debug` class to outline every hotspot in dashed red — rs17's `--debug` note in the docstring refers to this runtime behaviour, not a build flag.
Sources: [rs17_build_site.py](/records_space/scripts/rs17_build_site.py#L83-L87), [home_template.html](/records_space/home_page/home_template.html#L59-L68), [home_template.html](/records_space/home_page/home_template.html#L137-L151)

## The Self-Contained Page Pattern
Both the explorer and the negatives page are **single-file applications**: the template is a complete styled document with placeholder markers where dynamic content goes, and the assembler injects everything — data, CSS, JS — before writing the standalone output. rs05 injects three JS modules (`condition_parser.js`, `records_space.js`, `try_panel.js`) by string replacement, asserting each placeholder appears once and that no module contains a stray `</script` that would break inlining. The record data travels as one compact JSON blob with arrays stored as **base64-encoded binary** (`records.bin`, `seqs.bin`) decoded in the browser, plus `params.json`, the in-browser approximation model, coverage quantiles, and example definitions.
Sources: [rs05_build_explorer.py](/records_space/scripts/rs05_build_explorer.py#L170-L196), [rs05_build_explorer.py](/records_space/scripts/rs05_build_explorer.py#L198-L211)

Before inlining, rs05 performs a **cross-format integrity check**: it reads the `conc` array out of `records.bin` at its recorded byte offset and compares every value against the `conc_v` column of the TSV plot table, asserting fewer than 1% of rows disagree. This guards against the silent failure mode where the binary export and the plot table were built from different dataset revisions — a real risk in a pipeline where artifacts cross machine boundaries via Colab downloads.
Sources: [rs05_build_explorer.py](/records_space/scripts/rs05_build_explorer.py#L156-L170)

> [!TIP]
> The JSON blob is emitted with `.replace("</", "<\\/")` before injection. Without this escape, any `</` sequence in the data could terminate the enclosing `<script>` element mid-blob and silently corrupt the standalone page — a classic pitfall of data-inlined single-file sites.

The **protein universe lens** shows how rs05 stitches independently computed layers together. It decodes the quantized `xyds` coordinates from `universe_data.json`, places each dataset record at a **sunflower offset** (radius ∝ √r, golden angle 2.39996 rad) around its sequence's position, clamps to [0,1], and registers the result as a sixth embedding lens (`umap_universe`) alongside the five core lenses. It also asserts the tools table's bit-mask length equals the record count before inlining it.
Sources: [rs05_build_explorer.py](/records_space/scripts/rs05_build_explorer.py#L19-L23), [rs05_build_explorer.py](/records_space/scripts/rs05_build_explorer.py#L181-L195)

```mermaid
flowchart TB
    subgraph TEMPLATES
        T1["explorer_template.html<br/>4 placeholders × 1"]
        T2["pu_template.html<br/>/*__DATA__*/null × 1"]
        T3["home_template.html<br/>5 placeholders × 1"]
    end
    subgraph CONTENT
        J["JS modules ×3<br/>(assert no &lt;/script inside)"]
        D["JSON blob<br/>base64 arrays + &lt;/ escaped"]
        M["pu_map.npz → JSON<br/>uint16 coords · bitset masks"]
        H["hotspots + chips<br/>pixel → % anchors"]
    end
    F1["page_fragment.html<br/>+ standalone records_space_explorer.html"]
    F2["pu_page/index.html"]
    F3["site/index.html"]

    T1 -->|rs05| F1
    J --> F1
    D --> F1
    T2 -->|rs16| F2
    M --> F2
    T3 -->|rs17| F3
    H --> F3
```

## Colab Orchestration Layer
The artifacts the assemblers consume are produced in **disposable Colab sessions** driven by two zsh scripts. `run_universe.sh` requests a GPU with a fallback chain (A100 → L4 → T4, stopping and retrying on quota errors), uploads `universe_ids.tsv`, the sequence table, and cached ESMC matrices, then launches `drv_universe.py` in the background while `mirror.sh` incrementally mirrors output shards back to the local machine until it observes the `ALL_DONE` sentinel. `run_export.sh` runs a CPU session for `drv_export.py`, polling `progress.log` every 8 seconds for `EXPORT_FINISHED`.
Sources: [run_universe.sh](/records_space/colab/run_universe.sh#L8-L31), [run_export.sh](/records_space/colab/run_export.sh#L21-L30)

| Downloaded artifact (via `run_export.sh`) | Consumed by | Role in the page |
|---|---|---|
| `records.bin` / `records_meta.json` | rs05 | per-record condition arrays for the try panel |
| `seqs.bin` / `seqs_meta.json` | rs05 | sequence sketches + embeddings for paste-recognition |
| `params.json`, `approx.json`, `coverage.json` | rs05 | distance weights, composition-regression approximation, coverage quantiles |
| `examples.json` | rs05 | built-in example experiments |
| `export_log.txt` | — | session progress log archived beside the artifacts |

Sources: [run_export.sh](/records_space/colab/run_export.sh#L25-L30), [rs05_build_explorer.py](/records_space/scripts/rs05_build_explorer.py#L170-L178)

Both scripts share the same hygiene rules: filter lines containing `colab.dev` (they carry session proxy tokens), wrap every CLI call in `timeout`, upload `rslib.py` alongside task code so Colab-side scripts share the local helper library, and always send `colab stop` at the end. The same CLI-based transport explains why rs13 exists: it parses Colab's `universe.npz` with a **hand-written stdlib NPY reader** (zipfile + struct, supporting float16/32, integers, booleans, and UTF-32 strings) because the build machine has no NumPy.
Sources: [run_universe.sh](/records_space/colab/run_universe.sh#L2-L7), [run_export.sh](/records_space/colab/run_export.sh#L15-L20), [rs13_universe_export.py](/records_space/scripts/rs13_universe_export.py#L1-L6), [rs13_universe_export.py](/records_space/scripts/rs13_universe_export.py#L13-L37)

## Rebuild Caveats
Three facts matter if you want to reproduce the site. First, the assemblers hard-code **machine-local absolute paths** (`ROOT`, `BASE`, `THEME`) pointing to OneDrive directories outside this repository, so the scripts document a process rather than serve as a runnable Makefile. Second, the README states explicitly that `out/rs_plot_table.tsv` and `out/rs_coords.tsv` — rs05's primary inputs — are not included, "so the page cannot be rebuilt from this folder alone"; the same applies to the `pu_page/` and `data/pu/` trees that rs16 references. Third, the committed `index.html`, `assets/*.webp`, `records_space/index.html`, and `records_space/negatives/index.html` are **build outputs**, not sources: editing them directly works for quick fixes but will be overwritten the next time rs17 runs.
Sources: [rs17_build_site.py](/records_space/scripts/rs17_build_site.py#L12-L19), [README.md](/records_space/README.md#L72-L77), [rs16_build_pu.py](/records_space/scripts/rs16_build_pu.py#L14-L17)

The practical maintenance loop therefore separates cleanly: **content changes** to home-page copy, theme, or hotspot geometry go through `home_template.html` and rs17's hotspot tables (with `?debug` to verify regions visually); **data refreshes** re-run the Colab drivers and then the local assemblers; and **explorer behaviour** changes live in `explorer/js/*.js`, which rs05 re-inlines on every build. rs16's `summary.json` output doubles as a build report, recording protein counts, role distribution, set-pair overlaps, and how many manifest entries were newly embedded.
Sources: [rs17_build_site.py](/records_space/scripts/rs17_build_site.py#L44-L87), [rs16_build_pu.py](/records_space/scripts/rs16_build_pu.py#L84-L95), [home_template.html](/records_space/home_page/home_template.html#L137-L151)

## Where to Go Next
To see the pages this pipeline produces in action, start with the [Interactive Explorer Tour](4-interactive-explorer-tour), then dig into the distance model that rs05 inlines as parameters in [Record Map Distance Model](19-record-map-distance-model). The negatives page assembled by rs16 is explained in [Negatives and Protein Universe](20-negatives-and-protein-universe), and the condition vocabulary behind the hotspot links and filters is documented in [Loading Records by System](3-loading-records-by-system).

# Hyperparameter Grid Reference



Every experiment in OpenPhase is described by two things: a **sweep axis** (which system, which split, which embedding) and a set of **module-level defaults** (learning rates, loss weights, diffusion schedules). This page is the single consolidated catalog of both. It lists every tunable value that appears in the repository, where it is defined, and how the layers compose — so you can reproduce a specific grid cell or extend the sweep without re-reading every training script.

Sources: [params_all.yaml](params_all.yaml#L1-L32), [meta_config.py](meta_config.py#L38-L40)

## Three Layers of Configuration

Hyperparameters are not stored in one place; they are organized in three verifiable layers. The **sweep layer** (`params_all.yaml`) declares the categorical axes of the experiment space. The **validation layer** (`meta_config.py`) gates embedding names through Pydantic validators before they reach a dataset. The **execution layer** is per-module: benchmark drivers (`task1.py`, `task2.py`) take the sweep axes as function arguments and pin their own optimizer settings, while the generative modules (`Discrete/`, `ldm/`) carry self-contained configuration blocks (OmegaConf / argparse). Notably, `task1.py` contains the YAML load commented out (`# params = yaml.safe_load(f)`), confirming that the YAML serves as the sweep's documentation of record rather than an input consumed at runtime — the axes are passed explicitly to each baseline function.

```mermaid
flowchart TD
    G["params_all.yaml<br/>6 sweep axes"] --> V["meta_config.py<br/>MetaEmbeddingConfig validators"]
    E["meta_embed.py<br/>pooling · max_length=2048"] --> V
    V --> DB["zhanglab datasets<br/>DB1Dataset · DB3Dataset"]
    DB --> T1["task1.py<br/>AdaBoost · Droppler · CondFormer"]
    DB --> T2["task2.py<br/>PhaseCVAE"]
    DD["Discrete/training.py<br/>OmegaConf config"] --> UN["UNet + ProteinDiffusionModel<br/>MC-DDIM ensemble"]
    LD["ldm/utils/training.py<br/>argparse defaults"] --> JT["JTAE + ConDiff<br/>GaussianDiffusionTrainer"]
```

Sources: [params_all.yaml](params_all.yaml#L1-L32), [meta_config.py](meta_config.py#L5-L40), [task1.py](task1.py#L21-L23), [meta_embed.py](meta_embed.py#L17-L45)

## The Experiment Sweep Axes

`params_all.yaml` declares exactly six categorical axes. Together they define a raw grid of 7 × 7 × 3 × 2 × 3 × 3 = **2,646 combinations**; in practice, protein-only systems do not consume `dna_rna_method`, so the effective space is smaller per-system. The `system_name` values use the dataset-level naming (`protein(1)`, `protein(2) + RNA`, …) that `DB1Dataset` asserts against, which is distinct from the data-directory naming (`protein`, `protein_RNA`, …) used by the merged loaders.

| Axis | Values | Count |
|---|---|---|
| `system_name` | `protein(1)`, `protein(2)`, `protein(3)`, `protein(1) + DNA`, `protein(2) + DNA`, `protein(1) + RNA`, `protein(2) + RNA` | 7 |
| `split_method` | `random`, `phase_label_stratified`, `temperature_stratified`, `component_concentration_stratified`, `ionic_strength_stratified`, `crowding_agent_stratified`, `pH_stratified` | 7 |
| `protein_method` | `rnapsec_protein`, `esmc`, `mtdp` | 3 |
| `dna_rna_method` | `rnapsec_rna`, `dictionary` | 2 |
| `condition_method` | `rnapsec_condition`, `rnapsec_condition_class`, `droppler` | 3 |
| `task` | `task1`, `task2`, `task3` | 3 |

The repository root ships explicit drivers for `task1` and `task2`, while `task3` in the grid points at the generative benchmarks whose configurations live in the `Discrete/` and `ldm/` modules rather than in a root-level script. All seven `split_method` values are consumed verbatim by `dataset.get_idx_split(split_method=...)` in the Task 1 baselines.

Sources: [params_all.yaml](params_all.yaml#L1-L32), [task1.py](task1.py#L74-L77)

## Embedding Vocabulary and Defaults

Before any dataset is built, embedding names pass through `MetaEmbeddingConfig`. Each field has a validator with an explicit allowed set, and a value outside the set raises `ValueError` immediately — this is the gate that keeps the sweep axes consistent with what the embedding code can actually produce. Note that the **class field defaults** and the **factory function defaults** disagree on the protein axis: the class defaults to `esmc`, while `create_meta_config()` defaults to `mtdp`. Because every driver in `task1.py` builds its config through the factory, the effective default protein embedding across benchmarks is `mtdp`.

> [!TIP]
> When constructing configs programmatically, remember that `MetaEmbeddingConfig()` alone gives `esmc` but `create_meta_config()` gives `mtdp`. Benchmark scripts always call the factory, so the factory defaults are the de facto reference values.

| Field | Class default | Factory default | Allowed values |
|---|---|---|---|
| `protein_embedding` | `esmc` | `mtdp` | `esmc`, `mtdp`, `rnapsec_protein`, `seq2ind`, `seq2onehot` |
| `dna_rna_embedding` | `dictionary` | `dictionary` | `rnapsec_rna`, `dictionary` |
| `condition_embedding` | `droppler` | `droppler` | `droppler`, `rnapsec_condition`, `rnapsec_condition_class` |

Two auxiliary embedding-side hyperparameters also apply whenever embeddings are (re)computed: the ESM Cambrian path tokenizes with `max_length=2048` and pools residue states with `tensor_pooling`, which accepts exactly `mean`, `max`, `sum`, `norm`, `prod`, or `median` (default `mean`).

Sources: [meta_config.py](meta_config.py#L8-L35), [meta_config.py](meta_config.py#L38-L40), [meta_embed.py](meta_embed.py#L17-L45), [meta_embed.py](meta_embed.py#L48-L82), [params_all.yaml](params_all.yaml#L17-L27)

## Task 1: Benchmark Baselines

`task1.py` hosts three outcome-prediction baselines, each with a self-contained hyperparameter block. All three receive the sweep axes (`system_name`, `split_method`, `protein_method`, `dna_rna_method`, `condition_method`) as arguments and construct their dataset through `create_meta_config`.

Sources: [task1.py](task1.py#L58-L68)

### AdaBoost + Optuna Search Space

The RNAPSEC-feature baseline is the only place in the repository with a *searched* hyperparameter space: Optuna samples from two categorical distributions and scores candidates with 5-fold cross-validated macro one-vs-rest ROC-AUC, running 32 trials in parallel (`n_jobs=32`).

| Parameter | Values | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `max_depth` | `5, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10, None` | depth of the `DecisionTreeClassifier` base estimator |
| `learning_rate` | `0.5, 1.0, 1.5, 2.0, 2.5` | AdaBoost boosting weight |
| `random_state` | `30` | fixed inside the model |
| cross-validation | `cv=5` | scored by macro OVR ROC-AUC |
| Optuna budget | `n_trials=32`, `n_jobs=32` | direction = maximize |

Features are the concatenated embedding + condition vector standardized with `StandardScaler` before search and refit.

Sources: [task1.py](task1.py#L40-L48), [task1.py](task1.py#L79-L84)

### Droppler Neural Baseline

The Droppler path bypasses the embedding pipeline for the protein axis (it integer-indexes residues directly, 20 amino acids + padding) but reuses the 14-dimensional condition vector (`temp`, `conc`, `crowd`, `salt`, `ph` columns) scaled by a pretrained scaler marshalled at `./droppler/marshalled/scaler.pickle`.

| Parameter | Value |
|---|---|
| `selfatt_RRN(nfea, nCond, hidden_size, num_layers, heads)` | `20, 14, 10, 2, 10` |
| epochs | `10` |
| batch_size | `1024` |
| weight_decay | `1e-4` |
| learning_rate | `3e-3` |

Sources: [task1.py](task1.py#L131-L137), [task1.py](task1.py#L157-L159), [task1.py](task1.py#L170), [task1.py](task1.py#L181-L185)

### CondFormer Encoder–Classifier

The `protein(1)`-only transformer baseline pairs a `Protein1SystemEncoder` with a `PhaseClassificationHead`, both fixed at 256 embedding dimensions with dropout 0.5, trained with full-batch Adam for 1,000 epochs under binary cross-entropy, checkpointing the best test-AUROC epoch.

| Parameter | Value |
|---|---|
| `embed_dim` | `256` |
| `dropout` | `0.5` (encoder and head) |
| optimizer | Adam, `lr=7e-4`, `weight_decay=7e-6` |
| epochs | `1000` |
| loss | binary cross-entropy |
| model selection | best test AUROC → `condformer_<system>_<split>_best.pth` |
| input dims | `protein_dim` ∈ {29, 1280, 1024}; `condition_dim` ∈ {4, 14} |

Sources: [task1.py](task1.py#L267-L277), [task1.py](task1.py#L291), [task1.py](task1.py#L318-L329), [task1.py](task1.py#L268-L269)

### Frozen-Encoder Regression Transfer

The DB2 IDR regression run initializes from a stored CondFormer checkpoint (default `condformer_protein(1)_random_best.pth`), freezes every encoder parameter via `requires_grad = False`, and splits data 50/50 with seed 42. Its dimension ternary maps `rnapsec_protein → 29`, `mtdp → 1280`, and everything else (`esmc`, `seq2onehot`) → `1152`.

Sources: [task1.py](task1.py#L351-L352), [task1.py](task1.py#L378), [task1.py](task1.py#L384-L397)

## Task 2: PhaseCVAE

The condition-inference VAE is parameterized by three loss weights — `alpha` (reconstruction), `beta` (KL), `gamma` (phase prediction) — alongside standard training knobs. It operates on the 2D concentration slice of the condition vector and evaluates phase diagrams on a regular 30 × 30 inference grid padded by a 10% margin, with grid labels imputed by 5-nearest-neighbor majority voting.

| Parameter | Default | Role |
|---|---|---|
| `latent_dim` / `hidden_dim` | `64` / `128` | VAE capacity |
| `num_epochs` / `learning_rate` | `100` / `1e-2` | Adam schedule |
| `alpha`, `beta`, `gamma` | `10.0`, `0.1`, `5.0` | loss weights |
| `batch_size` | `1024` | dataloader default |
| train/test split | `test_size=0.5`, seed `42` | stratified on phase label |
| LR scheduler | `ReduceLROnPlateau(patience=10, factor=0.5)` | |
| gradient clipping | `max_norm=1.0` | |
| phase-diagram grid | `num_points=30`, `margin=0.1` | 2D protein/RNA concentration plane |
| KNN grid labeling | `k=5` | majority-vote imputation |

All eight configuration values (`num_epochs`, `learning_rate`, `batch_size`, `alpha`, `beta`, `gamma`, plus the three inferred dimensions) are logged to SwanLab at training start, making each run self-describing.

Sources: [task2.py](task2.py#L255-L271), [task2.py](task2.py#L304-L310), [task2.py](task2.py#L312-L316), [task2.py](task2.py#L320-L336), [task2.py](task2.py#L362), [task2.py](task2.py#L52-L61), [task2.py](task2.py#L88-L91), [task2.py](task2.py#L115), [task2.py](task2.py#L203), [task2.py](task2.py#L43)

## Discrete Diffusion Configuration

The discrete sequence diffusion driver is configured through an OmegaConf block plus hardcoded builder functions — there are no CLI arguments, so the values below *are* the configuration. Data is `x_seq2onehot` (N, L, 21) with `c_droppler` conditions, split 10% test / 10% validation from the remainder with seed 42.

| Group | Parameter | Value |
|---|---|---|
| Training (`build_config`) | `batch_size` | `8` |
| Training | `num_steps` | `21,300` |
| Training | `lr` / `weight_decay` | `1e-4` / `1e-4` |
| Training | `use_scheduler` | `True` → `OneCycleLR(max_lr=lr, total_steps=num_steps)` |
| UNet | `T`, `ch`, `ch_mult` | `1000`, `64`, `[1, 2, 4]` |
| UNet | `num_res_blocks`, `dropout` | `2`, `0.1` |
| UNet | `cond_dim`, `num_classes` | `14`, `21` (20 AA + pad) |
| Diffusion wrapper | `timesteps`, `loss_type` | `100`, `"CE"` |
| Diffusion wrapper | `objective`, `noise_type` | `"pred_x0"`, `"marginal"` |
| Diffusion wrapper | `marginal_dist_path` | `train_marginal_x.pt` |
| Optimizer | Adam `betas` | `(0.95, 0.999)` |
| Prior model | ESM2 | `esm2_t33_650M_UR50D` |

Sampling-side hyperparameters live on the `Trainer` signature, and here the **builder overrides matter**: `build_trainer` passes `save_and_sample_every=1` (validate every epoch, not every 100) and `ddim_steps=500` (not the constructor default of 50), while `ensemble_num=50` Monte-Carlo samples per sequence are kept at the default for both validation and test. Gradients are clipped to norm 1.0 on every step.

> [!TIP]
> If you are reproducing discrete-diffusion runs, read `build_trainer`, not the `Trainer` docstring defaults: the effective DDIM step count is 500 and validation cadence is 1 epoch, both overriding the `Trainer.__init__` defaults of 50 and 100.

| Sampler parameter | `Trainer` default | Effective via `build_trainer` |
|---|---|---|
| `train_num_steps` | `200,000` | `21,300` (from config) |
| `save_and_sample_every` | `100` | `1` |
| `ddim_steps` | `50` | `500` |
| `ensemble_num` | `50` | `50` |
| `sample_method` | `"ddim"` | `"ddim"` |

Sources: [Discrete/training.py](Discrete/training.py#L525-L537), [Discrete/training.py](Discrete/training.py#L541-L566), [Discrete/training.py](Discrete/training.py#L570-L586), [Discrete/training.py](Discrete/training.py#L589-L624), [Discrete/training.py](Discrete/training.py#L627-L645), [Discrete/training.py](Discrete/training.py#L25-L43), [Discrete/training.py](Discrete/training.py#L400-L441), [Discrete/training.py](Discrete/training.py#L446-L523), [Discrete/training.py](Discrete/training.py#L88-L113)

## Latent Diffusion: JTAE and ConDiff

The latent-diffusion module exposes its entire configuration as argparse defaults in `ldm/utils/training.py`, grouped into three blocks. Training uses AdamW with a two-phase schedule: linear warmup over `n_epochs // 10` epochs ramping to `multiplier × base_lr`, followed by cosine annealing to zero over the full epoch budget. The validation split (10%) and seed (42) are fixed inside the loader call.

| Block | Parameter | Default |
|---|---|---|
| Training | `batch_size` / `lr` / `n_epochs` | `8` / `2e-5` / `100` |
| Training | `multiplier` (warmup) | `2.5` |
| Training | optimizer | AdamW, `weight_decay=1e-4` |
| Training | schedulers | warmup `warm_epoch = n_epochs // 10` → `CosineAnnealingLR(T_max=n_epochs, eta_min=0)` |
| Training | checkpointing | every 50 epochs |
| Model | `input_dim` / `latent_dim` | `1152` / `256` |
| Model | `hidden_dim` / `embedding_dim` | `512` / `512` |
| Model | `seq_len` / `num_labels` | `2048` / `2` |
| Model | `eta_val` / `gamma_val` / `sigma_val` | `0.001` / `1.0` / `1.5` |
| Model | `layers` / `probs` / `kernel_size` | `4` / `0.2` / `3` |
| Diffusion | `dif_T` | `1000` |
| Diffusion | `dif_beta_1` → `dif_beta_T` | `1e-4` → `0.028` |
| Diffusion | `dif_channel` / `dif_channel_mult` | `64` / `[1, 2, 4]` |
| Diffusion | `dif_res_blocks` / `dif_dropout` | `2` / `0.15` |

The ConDiff training entry point (`ldm/training.py`) consumes three of those diffusion values directly — `GaussianDiffusionTrainer(net_model, dif_beta_1, dif_beta_T, dif_T)` — and adds two configuration behaviors of its own: classifier-free guidance is simulated by zeroing the label tensor with probability `0.1` per batch, and the noise-prediction loss is normalized by the square of the batch size (`loss.sum() / B²`).

Sources: [ldm/utils/training.py](ldm/utils/training.py#L139-L170), [ldm/utils/training.py](ldm/utils/training.py#L66-L83), [ldm/Scheduler.py](ldm/Scheduler.py#L8-L17), [ldm/training.py](ldm/training.py#L21-L28), [ldm/training.py](ldm/training.py#L33-L34)

## Cross-Cutting Conventions

Several conventions repeat across every driver, and knowing them lets you predict values you have not yet looked up. Fixed seeds are `30` (AdaBoost model) and `42` (every train/test split, the Task 2 UMAP projection, and the discrete/LDM data loaders). Validation/test fractions follow two patterns: held-out 10%/10% for the generative modules versus a 50/50 split for PhaseCVAE and the regression transfer. Gradient clipping to `max_norm=1.0` appears in the discrete trainer, PhaseCVAE, and the ConDiff loop. Finally, embedding dimensionality is determined by the `protein_method`/`condition_method` axis through fixed ternary mappings in `task1.py`.

| Convention | Value | Where applied |
|---|---|---|
| `rnapsec_protein` width | 29 | physicochemical feature vector |
| `mtdp` width | 1280 | MTDP encoder output |
| `esmc` width | 1024 | CondFormer branch |
| `seq2onehot` / LDM `input_dim` | 1152 | regression branch, JTAE input |
| condition width | 4 (`rnapsec_condition`) vs 14 (`droppler`/class) | Task 1, discrete diffusion `cond_dim` |
| residue alphabet | 21 (20 AA + pad) | one-hot and `num_classes` |

Sources: [task1.py](task1.py#L268-L269), [task1.py](task1.py#L385-L386), [task1.py](task1.py#L42), [task2.py](task2.py#L43), [Discrete/training.py](Discrete/training.py#L598-L604), [ldm/utils/training.py](ldm/utils/training.py#L66-L71)

## Reproducing a Grid Cell

To reproduce a specific experiment: pick the six axis values from `params_all.yaml`, confirm the embedding triple passes `MetaEmbeddingConfig` validation (or override through `create_meta_config`), then call the matching driver with its documented defaults from the tables above. For deeper background on what each configuration controls, continue with [Condition Inference with PhaseCVAE](9-condition-inference-with-phasecvae) for the Task 2 loss weights, [Split Strategies and Metrics](10-split-strategies-and-metrics) for the seven split methods, [Embedding Configuration Matrix](11-embedding-configuration-matrix) and [Condition Feature Engineering](13-condition-feature-engineering) for the embedding axes, and [Discrete Diffusion Foundations](14-discrete-diffusion-foundations), [Marginal Transition Matrices](15-marginal-transition-matrices), [Conditional UNet Denoiser](16-conditional-unet-denoiser), and [Latent Diffusion with JTAE](17-latent-diffusion-with-jtae) for the generative configuration blocks cataloged here.
